@@ -0,0 +1,441 @@
+# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://recipes.vllm.ai/recipe.schema.json
+meta:
+  title: "Kimi-K3.1-Pro"
+  slug: "kimi-k3.1-pro"
+  provider: "Moonshot AI"
+  description: "2.8T-parameter native multimodal MoE with Kimi Delta Attention, sparse MLA, and a 1M-token context window"
+  date_added: 2026-11-02
+  date_updated: 2026-11-04
+  tasks:
+    - multimodal
+    - text
+  performance_headline: "TP8 on two GB300 trays or one B300 node, or one MI355X node, for the MXFP4 checkpoint"
+  related_recipes:
+    - "moonshotai/Kimi-K3"
+  default_hardware: gb300
+  hardware:
+    gb300: verified
+    810e: verified
+    m890: verified
+
+model:
+  model_id: "moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro"
+  min_vllm_version: "nightly"
+  nightly_required: true
+  install:
+    docker:
+      note: "Use `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31` (multi-arch; CUDA 13 / cu130 build only). For CUDA 13.4 (Rubin) use `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31-cu134`. On MI355X use `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31`."
+    pip:
+      note: "Use a K3.1-enabled vLLM nightly after the integration lands."
+  architecture: moe
+  parameter_count: "2.8T"
+  active_parameters: "16 experts/token + shared (of 896 routed)"
+  context_length: 1048576
+  base_args:
+    - "--trust-remote-code"
+
+features:
+  tool_calling:
+    description: "Enable automatic tool choice with the Kimi K3 tool-call parser."
+    args:
+      - "--enable-auto-tool-choice"
+      - "--tool-call-parser"
+      - "kimi_k3"
+  reasoning:
+    description: "Parse Kimi K3 reasoning output separately from the final answer."
+    args:
+      - "--reasoning-parser"
+      - "kimi_k3"
+  spec_decoding:
+    description: "Use DSpark speculative decoding with the Kimi-K3.1 draft."
+    # The K3.1 DSpark draft (5 layers), not the K3 draft.
+    args:
+      - "--speculative-config"
+      - '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark-preview","num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
+    hardware_overrides:
+      # MI355X runs the draft on ROCM_AITER_MLA, and the draft's FP8 KV assumes
+      # an FP8 target KV. 5 draft tokens is the AgentX TP8 preset's value.
+      mi355x:
+        args:
+          - "--kv-cache-dtype"
+          - "fp8"
+          - "--speculative-config"
+          - '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark-preview","num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
+  text_only:
+    description: "Skip the vision encoder for text-only workloads; frees its memory for KV cache."
+    args:
+      - "--language-model-only"
+  low_latency_decode:
+    label: "Low-latency decode"
+    description: "Run decode steps on the fused CuTe DSL decode path (latency_specialized), which covers the sparse attention layers. Fastest at low concurrency; needs FULL decode CUDA graphs."
+    # Qualified at TP8 and TP8 + DCP8 without expert parallelism.
+    strategies:
+      - single_node_tp
+      - multi_node_tp
+    hardware:
+      ppu: unsupported
+    args:
+      - "--additional-config"
+      - '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}'
+  nvfp4_kv_cache:
+    label: "NVFP4 KV cache"
+    description: "Store the MLA latent in NVFP4 instead of FP8 for about 1.5x the KV cache tokens; the indexer keys stay FP8."
+    hardware:
+      ppu: unsupported
+    args:
+      - "--kv-cache-dtype"
+      - "nvfp4_ds_mla"
+
+opt_in_features:
+  - spec_decoding
+  - text_only
+  - low_latency_decode
+  - nvfp4_kv_cache
+
+variants:
+  default:
+    precision: mxfp4
+    # 1561 GB of safetensors x 1.2.
+    vram_minimum_gb: 1874
+    supported_hardware: [b300, gb300, mi355x, 810e, m890]
+    description: "MXFP4 routed-expert weights (~1.56 TB on disk); attention, shared experts and the vision tower stay in BF16."
+    hardware_overrides:
+      810e:
+        docker_image: "egslingjun-registry.cn-wulanchabu.cr.aliyuncs.com/egslingjun-tmp/inference-xpu-pytorch:kimi-k3.1-pro-vllm0.32.0-cuda13.0-pytorch2.13.0-20261103"
+        docker_serve_command: "vllm serve"
+        install: { pip: false }
+      m890:
+        docker_image: "egslingjun-registry.cn-wulanchabu.cr.aliyuncs.com/egslingjun-tmp/inference-xpu-pytorch:kimi-k3.1-pro-vllm0.32.0-cuda13.0-pytorch2.13.0-20261103"
+        docker_serve_command: "vllm serve"
+        install: { pip: false }
+      # Day-0 ROCm 10.0 image published with the release.
+      mi355x:
+        docker_image: "vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31"
+
+compatible_strategies:
+  - single_node_tp
+  - single_node_tep
+  - multi_node_tp
+  - pd_cluster
+
+strategy_hardware:
+  multi_node_tep:
+    810e: supported
+    m890: supported
+  single_node_tp:
+    810e: unsupported
+    m890: unsupported
+  single_node_tep:
+    810e: unsupported
+    m890: unsupported
+  multi_node_tp:
+    810e: unsupported
+    m890: unsupported
+  pd_cluster:
+    810e: unsupported
+    m890: unsupported
+
+# One B300 or MI355X node (8 GPUs) or two GB300 trays (2 x 4 GPUs) hold the checkpoint.
+strategy_min_gpus:
+  single_node_tp: 8
+  single_node_tep: 8
+  multi_node_tp: 8
+  810e: 32
+  m890: 32
+
+default_strategy: single_node_tp
+
+hardware_overrides:
+  blackwell:
+    extra_args:
+      - "--load-format"
+      - "fastsafetensors"
+    extra_env:
+      # Loading ~1.56 TB of weights from network storage can take over 20 minutes.
+      VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S: "3600"
+  amd:
+    extra_env:
+      VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER: "1"
+      SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU: "1"
+      VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2: "1"
+      # K3.1 has no torch.compile submodule, so only breakable graphs can
+      # capture the prefill sizes. They cost about 0.2 GiB of graph pool per
+      # capture size, so keep the capture list to the sizes you really use.
+      VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH: "1"
+      # Loading ~1.56 TB of weights and the first AITER JIT builds take a while.
+      VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S: "7200"
+
+presets:
+  mi355x_agentx:
+    label: "AgentX TP8"
+    hardware: mi355x
+    strategy: single_node_tp
+    workload: "Agentic (InferenceX AgentX)"
+    description: "Concurrency 48 on one MI355X node: TP8 with DCP8, the K3.1 DSpark draft, host KV offload and the reduced-precision knobs of the best-performance band."
+    select:
+      frontend: python
+      features: { spec_decoding: true, text_only: true }
+      kv_offload: simple
+    args:
+      - "--load-format"
+      - "fastsafetensors"
+      - "--max-model-len"
+      - "1048576"
+      - "--enable-prefix-caching"
+      - "--kv-cache-dtype"
+      - "fp8"
+      - "--stream-interval"
+      - "10"
+      - "--decode-context-parallel-size"
+      - "8"
+      - "--dcp-comm-backend"
+      - "a2a"
+      - "--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size"
+      - "1"
+      - "--prefix-match-unit"
+      - "64"
+      - "--max-num-seqs"
+      - "48"
+      - "--max-num-batched-tokens"
+      - "10240"
+      - "--gpu-memory-utilization"
+      - "0.92"
+      - "--attention-config"
+      - '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'
+      - "--additional-config"
+      - '{"kda_prefill_backend":"fused"}'
+      # Online FP8 per-channel for the KDA input projections only; routed
+      # experts keep their MXFP4 weights.
+      - "--quantization-config"
+      - '{"targets":{"*in_proj_qkvgfab":"fp8_per_channel"}}'
+      # The decode batches (48 requests x (1 + 5 draft tokens), so 6 to 288 in
+      # steps of 6), then the prefill sizes up to --max-num-batched-tokens.
+      - "--compilation-config"
+      - '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":10240,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,18,24,30,36,42,48,54,60,66,72,78,84,90,96,102,108,114,120,126,132,138,144,150,156,162,168,174,180,186,192,198,204,210,216,222,228,234,240,246,252,258,264,270,276,282,288,320,352,384,416,448,480,512,640,768,896,1024,1280,1536,1792,2048,2560,3072,3584,4096,4608,5120,6144,6400,7168,8192,8704,10240]}'
+    env:
+      VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER: "1"
+      VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_QUEUE_SIZE: "-1"
+      VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING: "asm"
+      # Verify the draft tokens with the AITER assembly DCP kernel.
+      VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY: "asm"
+      VLLM_ROCM_DCP_AITER_ALLGATHER: "1"
+      VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FLYDSL_SPARSE_MLA: "1"
+      # AITER reads its own variable for the same kernels.
+      AITER_FLYDSL_SPARSE_MLA: "1"
+      VLLM_ROCM_DSA_DCP_GLOBAL_KEY_PREFILL: "1"
+      VLLM_ROCM_DSA_DCP_ROWSHARD_PREFILL: "1"
+      VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A: "0"
+      VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER: "0"
+      VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER: "0"
+      # MoE stage-2 sums the per-route outputs through MXFP8 instead of BF16.
+      AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8: "1"
+      # Lossy: tensor-parallel all-reduces of 16 MiB and more go through INT4.
+      VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION: "INT4"
+      VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MIN_SIZE_BYTES_MB: "16"
+      # As in the benchmark lane.
+      PYTHONHASHSEED: "42"
+    # The Simple option's connector (SimpleCPUOffloadConnector, kv_both,
+    # lazy_offload false) with the lane's 1799 GB of host DRAM split per rank.
+    json_args:
+      "--kv-transfer-config": { kv_connector_extra_config: { cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank: 224875000000 } }
+    runbook: |
+      The single-node MI355X TP8 AgentX configuration at concurrency 48, from the K3.1 best-performance band. It is a BF16 serving config plus three reduced-precision knobs. It serves text with tool-call and reasoning parsers, using DCP8/A2A.
+
+      **Serving config.**
+      - **`--max-num-seqs 48` and capture sizes 6 to 10240.** At concurrency 48, decode batches are at most 48 requests × 6 rows (1 + 5 draft tokens), so the sizes 6 to 288 in steps of 6 cover every decode step exactly. The list then continues from 320 up to 10240, the value of `--max-num-batched-tokens`, to cover the prefill steps.
+      - **`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`.** K3.1 has no `torch.compile` submodule, so vLLM resolves `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and captures decode only. Breakable graphs are what let it capture the prefill sizes above 288 as well, so the AMD profile turns them on. They cost graph memory, which comes out of the KV cache: with the old 2-to-576 list (`--max-num-seqs 96`) they took 63.1 GiB and the server did not start. Keep the capture list to the sizes the workload really uses.
+      - **`--max-num-batched-tokens 10240`.** With prefix caching, the hybrid KV manager ends every non-final prefill chunk on a block boundary. In this preset (with the dense MLA DSpark draft sharing the block row) K3.1's packed DSA block is 1152 tokens, so after the decode rows a chunk floors to 9216 tokens (6912 at 8192).
+      - **`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`** gives more KV. Keep at least about 6 GiB free per GPU.
+      - **The indexer key cache is MXFP4** (`indexer_kv_dtype`). AITER needs padded FP4 indexer pages for it. Stock AITER asserts on the page stride at startup.
+      - `ROCM_AITER_FA` is named as the MLA prefill backend, which ROCm already picks first. `VLLM_ROCM_DCP_AITER_ALLGATHER=1`, the FlyDSL sparse-MLA kernels and the DSA DCP prefill paths are on. `kda_prefill_backend: fused` prefills the KDA layers with the fused gfx950 kernel.
+      - **Spec decoding** (the Spec decoding feature, on in this preset) uses the K3.1 DSpark draft (5 layers, not the K3 draft) with 5 tokens, `ROCM_AITER_MLA` attention, FP8 KV, probabilistic drafting and vLLM's default (standard) rejection sampler. The draft is [`Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark-preview`](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark-preview).
+      - The **Simple** KV-offload option gets 224,875,000,000 bytes of host DRAM per rank. Size `cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank` to your host.
+
+      **Reduced precision (best-performance band).** The serving config keeps linear layers, MoE combine and all-reduce in BF16. This preset adds:
+      - `--quantization-config '{"targets":{"*in_proj_qkvgfab":"fp8_per_channel"}}'`: only the KDA input projections are quantized online to FP8 per channel.
+      - `AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1`: the FlyDSL MoE down projection writes its per-route outputs as MXFP8 before they are summed.
+      - `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4` with `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MIN_SIZE_BYTES_MB=16`: all-reduces of 16 MiB and more use the lossy INT4 codec. To serve with BF16 all-reduce, unset both.
+
+      Drop all three for BF16 precision.
+
+      **Environment outside the builder.** The lane also sets `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` (the SiTUv2 path does not read it), `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200` for long agentic prefills, `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1`, `HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=0`, and `HSA_SCRATCH_SINGLE_LIMIT_ASYNC=25769803776` (24 GiB), which caps a single asynchronous scratch allocation.
+
+      ### Throughput measurement only (synthetic acceptance)
+
+      The AgentX runs replace real verification with synthetic acceptance at the golden acceptance length for 5 draft tokens, 3.62. Only `--speculative-config` changes:
+
+      ```bash
+      --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark-preview","num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.62}'
+      ```
+
+      Synthetic acceptance skips real verification. Never use it to serve users or to evaluate accuracy.
+
+# DCP8 over the TP8 group (one B300 node or two GB300 trays).
+decode_context_parallel:
+  sizes:
+    b300: [8]
+    gb300: [8]
+  match_tp: true
+
+strategy_overrides:
+  multi_node_tep:
+    hardware_overrides:
+      810e:
+        extra_args:
+          - "--gpu-memory-utilization"
+          - "0.9"
+          - "--max-num-seqs"
+          - "256"
+          - "--max-model-len"
+          - "auto"
+          - "--disable-custom-all-reduce"
+          - "--no-enable-prefix-caching"
+          - "--moe-backend"
+          - "ppu_deep_gemm_w4a16"
+        extra_env:
+          VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S: "3600"
+          DG_USE_MOE_DYNAMIC_TILE: "1"
+          PCCL_NET_PLUGIN_ENABLE: "1"
+          NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: "eth0"
+          NCCL_DEBUG: "WARN"
+          NCCL_IB_HCA: "fic2,vsolar"
+      m890:
+        extra_args:
+          - "--tensor-parallel-size"
+          - "8"
+          - "--data-parallel-size"
+          - "4"
+          - "--all2all-backend"
+          - "deepep_low_latency"
+          - "--gpu-memory-utilization"
+          - "0.9"
+          - "--max-num-seqs"
+          - "32"
+          - "--max-model-len"
+          - "auto"
+          - "--disable-custom-all-reduce"
+          - "--no-enable-prefix-caching"
+        extra_env:
+          VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S: "3600"
+          DG_USE_MOE_DYNAMIC_TILE: "1"
+          VLLM_SAIL_DENSE_BF16_DEEPGEMM: "1"
+          VLLM_SAIL_DEEPGEMM_MOE_TP_FUSED: "1"
+          VLLM_SAIL_DEEPGEMM_MOE_FUSED_ACT_QUANT: "1"
+          VLLM_DEEPEPLL_RECV_HOOK: "0"
+          VLLM_DEEPEP_LOW_LATENCY_USE_MNNVL: "1"
+          DEEPEP_COMBINE_TOKEN_BALANCED: "1"
+  # TEP on one B300 node: experts on MegaMoE, which dispatches tokens over
+  # NVLink one-sided all-to-all.
+  single_node_tep:
+    extra_args:
+      - "--moe-backend"
+      - "deep_gemm_mega_moe"
+      - "--all2all-backend"
+      - "flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided"
+
+  # PD pools: a TP8 prefill pool with expert parallelism (one B300 node or two
+  # GB300 trays) and a DEP16 decode pool — TP1 x DP16 with expert parallelism
+  # (two B300 nodes or four GB300 trays). NIXL moves the KDA short-conv state
+  # in three reads, which needs the DS conv state layout.
+  pd_cluster:
+    env:
+      VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT: "DS"
+    prefill:
+      nodes:
+        b300: 1    # 1 B300 node = 8 GPUs
+        gb300: 2   # 2 GB300 trays = 8 GPUs
+      parallelism: tep
+      tp: 8
+    decode:
+      nodes:
+        b300: 2    # 2 B300 nodes = 16 GPUs
+        gb300: 4   # 4 GB300 trays = 16 GPUs
+      parallelism: dep
+      tp: 1
+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  Kimi-K3.1 keeps the Kimi-K3 layout (Kimi Delta Attention, 896 routed experts with 16 active
+  per token, a latent MoE projection and a vision encoder) and adds sparse
+  attention (DSA, top-2048 indexer) to 24 of its MLA layers. The checkpoint ships MXFP4
+  routed-expert weights; everything else is BF16.
+
+  The baseline is the simplest working setup on NVIDIA: one tensor-parallel group of 8 GPUs,
+  either two GB300 trays or one B300 node. Throughput was not tuned.
+
+  On MI355X, one node takes the same TP8 layout with the AMD profile's AITER environment, in the
+  day-0 `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31` image. So far only the
+  [AgentX TP8](#preset-mi355x_agentx) configuration has run on MI355X: the tuned single-node AgentX
+  configuration for concurrency 48, with DCP8, the K3.1 DSpark draft and host KV offload.
+
+  On Zhenwu PPUs, the default MXFP4 checkpoint runs without speculative decoding on
+  two 16-PPU 810E nodes with TP32 / EP32, or four 8-PPU M890 nodes with TP8 / DP4 / EP32.
+  On 810E, `ppu_deep_gemm_w4a16` loads the checkpoint with a W4A16 compute path.
+  Use the PPU image specified for each hardware configuration.
+
+  ## Tensor + expert parallelism
+
+  On one B300 node, the **Tensor + Expert Parallel** strategy keeps attention at TP8 and runs
+  the routed experts with expert parallelism on the MegaMoE kernel. It has the lowest
+  long-prompt time to first token of the single-node layouts: a single 340K-token prompt
+  prefills in about 10 s, against about 15 s at plain TP8 (8x B300, one request at a time,
+  pre-release checkpoint).
+
+  ## Long context: decode context parallelism
+
+  The **Decode Context Parallelism** row shards the MLA latent and indexer-key caches across
+  the 8 GPUs of the TP group instead of replicating them, so DCP8 holds about 7x the KV cache
+  tokens of TP8 (about 18.5M vs 2.6M tokens with FP8 KV on 8x B300). Prefill is as fast as
+  at TP8. Decode steps are 7–25% slower than TP8 at the same batch, so use DCP when KV
+  capacity is the limit: very long contexts or many long-lived agentic sessions.
+
+  ## Low-latency decode
+
+  The **Low-latency decode** feature switches decode steps to a fused CuTe DSL path tuned for
+  small batches; prefill and mixed steps still run the default path. On 8x B300 at TP8 it cuts
+  the decode step by 1.6–1.7x at batch 1 and 1.2–1.3x at batch 32–64. Under DCP8 it brings decode
+  to within 6% of TP8. It requires the V2 model runner and FULL decode CUDA graphs (the
+  defaults), TP8 or TP8 + DCP8, and no expert parallelism in this recipe.
+
+  ## NVFP4 KV cache
+
+  The **NVFP4 KV cache** feature stores the MLA latent in NVFP4 (352 bytes per token per layer
+  instead of 576) and holds about 1.5x the KV cache tokens of FP8. The indexer keys stay FP8,
+  so the top-2048 token selection is unchanged. GSM8K matched FP8 on 8x GB300 (96.1% vs 96.2%);
+  long-context accuracy has not been measured yet.
+
+  ## Prefill/decode disaggregation
+
+  The **Prefill/Decode Disaggregation** strategy runs one TP8 prefill pool (with expert
+  parallelism) and one DEP16 decode pool (TP1 x DP16 with expert parallelism), and decode
+  pulls each request's KV from prefill over NIXL. Every PD worker sets
+  `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`: NIXL transfers the Kimi Delta Attention conv state in three
+  reads, which needs that layout, and the NIXL connector refuses to start without it.
+
+  ## KV cache offloading
+
+  The **Simple** option on the KV Offload row adds `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, a host-DRAM
+  prefix tier for each GPU. Under Prefill/Decode Disaggregation it is added to the prefill pool
+  only, next to NIXL in a MultiConnector; decode keeps plain NIXL. The tier pins
+  `cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank` of host memory for every GPU, so size it from the host DRAM that
+  is free after the engines are up. The tested GB300 prefill workers used 128 GiB per GPU
+  (512 GiB per tray).
+
+  ## Client usage
+
+  ```bash
+  curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -d '{
+      "model": "moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro",
+      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain sparse attention in two sentences."}],

+

+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.mhc.triton import mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_triton
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc import (

+    MHCPreDelayedOp,
+)

+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import aux_stream
+
+MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS = 128
+

+    config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
+    return (
+        get_cdna_version() == 4
+        and HAS_AITER_MHC_FUSED_POST_PRE_DELAYED_RMS_NORM
+        and config.hc_mult == 4
+        and not vllm_config.parallel_config.use_ubatching
+    )

+
+class MHCOverlapStream:
+    """The global aux stream with the fork and join events of the overlap.
+
+    Every fork and join waits on its event before the next records it, so all
+    layers share the two events.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        stream = aux_stream()
+        assert stream is not None
+        self.stream = stream
+        self._fork_event = torch.cuda.Event()
+        self._join_event = torch.cuda.Event()
+
+    def fork(self) -> None:
+        self._fork_event.record()
+        self.stream.wait_event(self._fork_event)
+
+    def join(self) -> None:
+        self._join_event.record(self.stream)
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_event(self._join_event)
+

+def shard(shape: tuple[int, ...], shard_id) -> torch.Tensor:
+    weight = torch.ones(shape)
+    weight.shard_id = shard_id

+    assert layer.pop_missing_shards() == []

+    assert layer.pop_missing_shards() == ["bias.k", "bias.v"]

[KVConnector][Mooncake] Add per-GPU device names for MooncakeStoreConnector (#65076)

Signed-off-by: whx-sjtu <xiaowang990929@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Co-authored-by: Shanshan Shen <467638484@qq.com>

files.patch:
@@ -56,6 +56,10 @@ Create a JSON configuration file (e.g., `mooncake_config.json`):
   Store provider owns the memory pool and (optionally) the SSD tier.
 - `protocol`: Use `"rdma"` for best performance. `"tcp"` works as a fallback.
   `"nvlink"` is used by the opt-in [EGM deployment](#standalone-egm-over-nvlink).
+- `device_name_per_gpu`: Optional list of RDMA device names indexed by
+  physical GPU ID, such as `["rdma0", "rdma1", ...]`. Each rank's store client
+  uses only its own GPU's entry, which may list several devices separated by
+  commas. Set it instead of `device_name` to give each GPU its local NIC.
 - `global_segment_size`: CPU memory contributed to the distributed pool (per
   GPU). Must be `> 0` in `embedded` mode and `0` in `standalone-store` mode.
 - `local_buffer_size`: Private buffer for this node's own operations (per GPU).

+def _device_name_for_current_gpu(config: MooncakeStoreConfig) -> str:
+    if config.device_name_per_gpu is None:

+    import torch

 ```
 
+For batch embeddings, create an `embeddings.jsonl` file with one request per line:
+
+```json
+{"custom_id":"embedding-1","method":"POST","url":"/v1/embeddings","body":{"model":"intfloat/multilingual-e5-small","input":"query: What is vLLM?","encoding_format":"float"}}
+```
+
+```bash
+vllm run-batch -i embeddings.jsonl -o results.jsonl \
+    --model intfloat/multilingual-e5-small
+```
+
+Each output keeps the request's `custom_id`. Successful embeddings appear in
+`response.body.data` with `response.status_code` set to `200` and `error` set to
+`null`. Check each output's status and error fields: a completed batch can
+contain failed requests.
+
 See [vllm run-batch](./run-batch.md) for the full reference of all available arguments.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The specialized decode's TP all-gather (``LamportAllGather``) at TP4.
+
+* ``accepts`` by size: 16-byte multiples up to the capacity.
+* Eager gathers of int32, BF16 and FP32 tensors whose sizes grow and shrink
+  from call to call (1 pack to the full capacity), one rank late each call,
+  bitwise against NCCL.
+* The Lamport sentinel word (FP32 negative zero, INT32_MIN) arrives as 0 on
+  every rank, the sending rank included.
+* CUDA graphs of three gathers of different sizes each, some with the ranks
+  skewed, replayed in a seeded random order with new contents every replay;
+  a device-side count of words that differ from the expected concatenation
+  must stay 0. A word left in the mailbox by an earlier call of another size
+  would show up here as a mismatch.
+
+Needs four SM100-family GPUs with NVLink multicast; about a minute. For a
+stress run, run this file as a module
+(``python -m tests.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_all_gather``)
+with ``--replays 2000000``. With ``--custom-all-gather`` it replays the same
+graphs on vLLM's custom all-gather (``CustomAllreduce.custom_all_gather``, the
+MNNVL Lamport kernel) instead and only counts the mismatched words: that
+kernel never waits for a rank's own multicast copy, and words of an earlier
+call can reach a later one.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import random
+import tempfile
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+TP = 4
+CAPACITY = 4 << 20  # bytes a rank, as the executor builds it
+REPLAYS = 2000
+LATE_CYCLES = 20_000
+SENTINEL = -(2**31)
+# Pack counts (16 bytes each) of the eager sequence: growing, shrinking, a
+# partial last CTA, one pack and the full capacity.
+EAGER_PACKS = (1, 37, 389, 128, 5000, 3, CAPACITY // 16, 2, 777, 1)
+# Words a rank of each graph's three gathers.
+GRAPH_WORDS = (
+    (4, 2800, 148),
+    (20000, 12, 2048),
+    (512, 8192, 4),
+    (CAPACITY // 4, 4, 64),
+)
+
+
+def _late(rank: int, step: int) -> None:
+    """Delay one rank per step, a different one each step."""
+    if rank == step % TP:
+        torch.cuda._sleep(LATE_CYCLES)
+
+
+def _random_words(generator, words: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Random int32 words, none of them the sentinel."""
+    x = torch.randint(
+        -(2**31),
+        2**31 - 1,
+        (words,),
+        generator=generator,
+        device="cuda",
+        dtype=torch.int64,
+    ).to(torch.int32)
+    return torch.where(x == SENTINEL, 1, x)
+
+
+def _check_accepts(all_gather):
+    assert not all_gather.accepts(torch.empty(0, device="cuda"))
+    assert not all_gather.accepts(torch.empty(2, device="cuda"))  # 8 bytes
+    assert all_gather.accepts(torch.empty(4, device="cuda"))
+    assert all_gather.accepts(torch.empty(CAPACITY // 4, device="cuda"))
+    assert not all_gather.accepts(torch.empty(CAPACITY // 4 + 4, device="cuda"))
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        all_gather(torch.empty(2, device="cuda"))
+
+
+def _check_eager(all_gather, rank):
+    from vllm.distributed import get_tp_group
+
+    group = get_tp_group()
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(rank)
+    for step, packs in enumerate(EAGER_PACKS):
+        words = _random_words(generator, packs * 4)
+        for dtype in (torch.int32, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32):
+            # One 16-byte pack a row.
+            x = words.view(dtype).view(packs, -1)
+            _late(rank, step)
+            got = all_gather(x)
+            want = group.all_gather(x, 0)
+            assert got.dtype == dtype and got.shape == want.shape, (packs, dtype)
+            assert torch.equal(got.view(torch.int32), want.view(torch.int32)), (
+                packs,
+                dtype,
+            )
+
+
+def _check_sentinel(all_gather, rank):
+    from vllm.distributed import get_tp_group
+
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(100 + rank)
+    x = _random_words(generator, 64)
+    x[rank::7] = SENTINEL
+    got = all_gather(x)
+    want = get_tp_group().all_gather(x, 0)
+    want = torch.where(want == SENTINEL, 0, want)
+    assert torch.equal(got, want)
+    negative_zero = torch.full((8,), -0.0, device="cuda")
+    gathered = all_gather(negative_zero)
+    assert torch.equal(gathered.view(torch.int32), torch.zeros_like(gathered).int())
+
+
+def _pattern(rank: int, kind: int, words: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """(rank, kind, index) as int32 bits, never the sentinel; the replay
+    counter goes into bits 20-25."""
+    index = torch.arange(words, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") & 0xFFFFF
+    return (rank << 28) | (kind << 26) | index
+
+
+def _check_replays(all_gather, rank, replays, stop=True):
+    """Gather graphs replayed in a random order; returns the mismatch count,
+    after the first 1000 replays with a mismatch if ``stop``."""
+    from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import graph_capture
+
+    counter = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    errors = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+    graphs = []
+    with graph_capture(device=torch.device("cuda")) as context:
+        for sizes in GRAPH_WORDS:
+            mine = [_pattern(rank, k, n) for k, n in enumerate(sizes)]
+            want = [
+                torch.cat([_pattern(r, k, n) for r in range(TP)])
+                for k, n in enumerate(sizes)
+            ]
+            inputs = [torch.empty_like(m) for m in mine]
+            for skew in (False, True):
+
+                def body(mine=mine, want=want, inputs=inputs, skew=skew):
+                    counter.add_(1)
+                    bits = (counter & 0x3F) << 20
+                    outs = []
+                    for kind in range(3):
+                        torch.add(mine[kind], bits, out=inputs[kind])
+                        if skew:
+                            torch.cuda._sleep(LATE_CYCLES * ((rank + kind) % TP))
+                        outs.append(all_gather(inputs[kind]))
+                    for kind in range(3):
+                        errors.add_((outs[kind] != want[kind] + bits).sum())
+
+                body()
+                graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+                with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=context.stream):
+                    body()
+                # The graph keeps raw pointers: keep its tensors alive too.
+                graphs.append((graph, (mine, want, inputs)))
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert not stop or errors.item() == 0, "eager warm-up"
+    order = random.Random(1234)
+    for start in range(0, replays, 1000):
+        for _ in range(min(1000, replays - start)):
+            graphs[order.randrange(len(graphs))][0].replay()
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        if stop and errors.item():
+            break
+    return int(errors.item())
+
+
+def _worker(rank: int, port: int, replays: int, skip_path: str, custom: bool) -> None:
+    from tests.utils import init_test_distributed_environment
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.distributed import cleanup_dist_env_and_memory, get_tp_group
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.ops.cute_dsl import LamportAllGather
+
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(rank)
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()), torch.inference_mode():
+        init_test_distributed_environment(TP, 1, rank, str(port), local_rank=rank)
+        ca_comm = getattr(get_tp_group().device_communicator, "ca_comm", None)
+        supported = torch.tensor(
+            [int(ca_comm is not None and bool(ca_comm.mnnvl_lamport_ag_multicast_ptr))]
+        )
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(
+            supported, torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MIN, get_tp_group().cpu_group
+        )
+        if not supported.item():
+            if rank == 0:
+                with open(skip_path, "w") as f:
+                    f.write("no NVLink multicast")
+            cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()
+            return
+        if custom:
+            assert ca_comm is not None
+
+            def all_gather(x):
+                # It takes floating-point inputs only; the int32 words pass
+                # bitwise as FP32.
+                out = ca_comm.custom_all_gather(x.view(torch.float32))
+                assert out is not None, x.nbytes
+                return out.view(x.dtype)
+
+        else:
+            all_gather = LamportAllGather(
+                rank_capacity_bytes=CAPACITY, device=torch.device("cuda", rank)
+            )
+            _check_accepts(all_gather)
+            _check_eager(all_gather, rank)
+            _check_sentinel(all_gather, rank)
+        errors = _check_replays(all_gather, rank, replays, stop=not custom)
+        total = torch.tensor([errors])
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(total, group=get_tp_group().cpu_group)
+        print(
+            f"rank {rank}: {replays} replays ({3 * replays} gathers) on the "
+            f"{'custom' if custom else 'Lamport'} all-gather, {errors} mismatched "
+            f"words here, {int(total.item())} on all ranks",
+            flush=True,
+        )
+        assert custom or total.item() == 0
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()
+
+
+def run(replays: int, custom: bool = False) -> str | None:
+    """Run the checks on four GPUs (only the replays on the custom all-gather
+    if ``custom``); returns why they were skipped, if so."""
+    from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port
+
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+        skip_path = os.path.join(tmp, "skipped")
+        torch.multiprocessing.spawn(
+            _worker, args=(get_open_port(), replays, skip_path, custom), nprocs=TP
+        )
+        if os.path.exists(skip_path):
+            with open(skip_path) as f:
+                return f.read()
+    return None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.distributed(num_gpus=4)
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100), reason="needs SM100"
+)
+def test_lamport_all_gather():
+    if torch.accelerator.device_count() < TP:
+        pytest.skip("needs four GPUs")
+    skipped = run(REPLAYS)
+    if skipped:
+        pytest.skip(skipped)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
+    parser.add_argument("--replays", type=int, default=REPLAYS)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--custom-all-gather",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="replay the graphs on vLLM's custom all-gather and count mismatches",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    skipped = run(args.replays, args.custom_all_gather)
+    print(f"skipped: {skipped}" if skipped else "done")

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""``decode_topk`` (``decode_topk_cute.py``) against ``torch.topk``.
+
+Token mode: each row's output must be an exact top-k of its BF16 logits in
+the kernel's key order (every index whose key exceeds the k-th largest key,
+then indices whose key equals it), or ``0 .. n-1`` and -1 for rows of at most
+k values. Rows cover the sampled path, short rows (the direct path), crowded
+and constant values, values rising toward the row's end (survivors in the last
+CTA), NaN and infinities, the forced direct path, and a sample that misses the
+row's top values. Block mode must
+select an exact top-k of the 8-token block maxima, as the stock
+``select_candidate_blocks`` on the upcast logits does, with the newest block
+pinned and -inf blocks written as -1.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.attention.decode_topk_cute import (  # noqa: E501
+    SAMPLES,
+    _resident_clusters,
+    cluster_for,
+    decode_topk,
+    supports_decode_topk,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (
+        current_platform.is_cuda() and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
+    ),
+    reason="needs an SM100-family GPU",
+)
+
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+WIDTH = 262144
+
+
+def order_keys(values: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The kernel's order-preserving key of each BF16 value, as int32."""
+    bits = values.view(torch.int16).int() & 0xFFFF
+    return torch.where(bits >= 0x8000, bits ^ 0xFFFF, bits ^ 0x8000)
+
+
+def make_logits(rows: int, kind: str, seed: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[rows, WIDTH] BF16 logits of one distribution."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(seed)
+    x = torch.randn(rows, WIDTH, device=DEVICE, generator=g)
+    if kind == "crowded":  # few distinct values: long exact ties
+        x = torch.randint(0, 6, (rows, WIDTH), device=DEVICE, generator=g).float()
+    elif kind == "constant":
+        x = torch.full((rows, WIDTH), 3.0, device=DEVICE)
+    elif kind == "rising":  # the largest values at the row's end
+        x = x * 0.1 + torch.linspace(0, 8, WIDTH, device=DEVICE)
+    elif kind == "special":
+        x[:, 7] = float("nan")
+        x[:, 1000::977] = float("inf")
+        x[:, 2000::991] = float("-inf")
+    return x.bfloat16()
+
+
+def check_tokens(logits: torch.Tensor, lengths: list[int], out: torch.Tensor, k: int):
+    """Assert each row's output is an exact top-k (module docstring)."""
+    for r, n in enumerate(lengths):
+        got = out[r]
+        if n <= k:
+            want = torch.arange(k, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.int32)
+            want[n:] = -1
+            assert torch.equal(got, want), f"row {r} (n {n})"
+            continue
+        assert int((got < 0).sum()) == 0 and int(got.max()) < n, (
+            f"row {r}: ids out of range"
+        )
+        assert got.unique().numel() == k, f"row {r}: repeated ids"
+        keys = order_keys(logits[r, :n])
+        kth = keys.topk(k).values[-1]
+        chosen = keys[got.long()]
+        assert int((chosen < kth).sum()) == 0, f"row {r}: a key below the k-th"
+        assert int((chosen > kth).sum()) == int((keys > kth).sum()), (
+            f"row {r}: missed a key above"
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["normal", "crowded", "constant", "rising", "special"])
+# One row, 8 CTAs a row (12), 4 CTAs a row (20), the most rows (64).
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [1, 12, 20, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("k", "fallback"), [(512, False), (2048, False), (2048, True)])
+def test_token_topk(kind, rows, k, fallback):
+    lengths_all = [
+        WIDTH,
+        0,
+        k - 1,
+        k,
+        k + 1,
+        5000,
+        8192,
+        8193,
+        30000,
+        162000,
+        99991,
+        250000,
+    ]
+    lengths = [lengths_all[(r * 5) % len(lengths_all)] for r in range(rows)]
+    logits = make_logits(rows, kind, rows * 31 + k)
+    assert supports_decode_topk(logits, rows, k, block_mode=False)
+    ends = torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    out = torch.full((rows, k), 7, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    decode_topk(logits, ends, out, block_mode=False, fallback=fallback)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    check_tokens(logits, lengths, out, k)
+
+
+def test_token_topk_strided_output_and_graph():
+    """A wider output buffer (row stride > k) and a CUDA graph replay on new
+    logits."""
+    rows, k = 12, 512
+    lengths = [162000, 140000, 600, 9000] * 3
+    logits = make_logits(rows, "normal", 1)
+    ends = torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    buffer = torch.full((rows, k + 64), 7, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    out = buffer[:, :k]
+    decode_topk(logits, ends, out, block_mode=False)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    check_tokens(logits, lengths, out, k)
+    assert torch.all(buffer[:, k:] == 7)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        decode_topk(logits, ends, out, block_mode=False)
+    logits.copy_(make_logits(rows, "rising", 2))
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    check_tokens(logits, lengths, out, k)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "rows,wide,cluster",
+    [(4, 2 * WIDTH, 8), (20, 2 * WIDTH, 8), (4, 4 * WIDTH, 16), (12, 4 * WIDTH, 16)],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fallback", [False, True])
+def test_wide_rows(rows, wide, cluster, fallback):
+    """Rows of up to 524,288 logits (the ratio-2 layers' width at a 1M
+    context), which only 8 CTAs a row hold, and of up to 1,048,576 (the
+    candidate source's), which take 16; at 20 and 12 rows more clusters than
+    a GB300 runs at once, so they run in waves."""
+    lengths = [
+        [wide, wide * 3 // 4 + 1, wide // 2 + 1, 9000][r % 4] for r in range(rows)
+    ]
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(11)
+    logits = (torch.randn(rows, wide, device=DEVICE, generator=g) - 1.5).bfloat16()
+    assert supports_decode_topk(logits, rows, 512, block_mode=False)
+    assert supports_decode_topk(logits, rows, 2048, block_mode=True)

+    out = torch.full((rows, 512), 7, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    decode_topk(logits, ends, out, block_mode=False, fallback=fallback)
+    blocks = torch.full((rows, 2048), 7, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    decode_topk(logits, ends, blocks, block_mode=True)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    check_tokens(logits, lengths, out, 512)

+        nblocks = (end + 7) // 8

+    nblocks = (end + 7) // 8

+    padded[:end] = logits[:end].float()

+    scores[nblocks - 1] = float("inf")

+    chosen = torch.full_like(ids, NEG_INF_KEY)
+    chosen[ids >= 0] = keys[valid.long()]
+    return chosen.sort().values

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""``sparse_mla_decode`` (``sparse_mla_cute.py``) against an FP32 reference.
+
+Each token attends to its own columns: the first 128 index the sliding-window
+pool and the rest the compressed pool, as storage offsets. The cases cover the
+widths of 1 to 5 chunks (128, a partial second chunk, 384, 512, 640), masked
+columns (-1 and columns past a token's length, including a token with no active
+column, whose output is zero), batches from one token to the most the kernel
+takes, sinks and none, and scales other than one. The tolerance allows for the
+probabilities' FP8 rounding (TRTLLM-gen's own error is of the same size).
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.attention.sparse_mla_cute import (  # noqa: E501
+    _max_tokens,
+    sparse_mla_decode,
+    supports_sparse_mla_cute,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (
+        current_platform.is_cuda() and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
+    ),
+    reason="needs an SM100-family GPU",
+)
+
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+H, D, SWA = 16, 512, 128
+SWA_ROWS, COMP_ROWS, PAGE = 1024, 8192, 64
+
+
+def fp8(shape: tuple[int, ...], std: float, g: torch.Generator) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Normal values of standard deviation ``std`` as FP8 E4M3."""
+    return (torch.randn(shape, device=DEVICE, generator=g) * std).to(
+        torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    )
+
+
+def make_case(tokens: int, width: int, seed: int) -> dict:
+    """Pools, indices with masked columns, and lengths for ``tokens`` tokens."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(seed)
+    swa_pool = fp8((SWA_ROWS // PAGE, PAGE, D), 1.0, g)
+    comp_pool = fp8((COMP_ROWS // PAGE, PAGE, D), 1.0, g)
+    swa = torch.randint(
+        0, SWA_ROWS, (tokens, min(width, SWA)), device=DEVICE, generator=g
+    )
+    columns = [swa]
+    if width > SWA:
+        columns.append(
+            torch.randint(
+                0, COMP_ROWS, (tokens, width - SWA), device=DEVICE, generator=g
+            )
+        )
+    indices = torch.cat(columns, dim=1).to(torch.int32)
+    drop = torch.rand(indices.shape, device=DEVICE, generator=g) < 0.05
+    indices[drop] = -1
+    lens = torch.full((tokens,), width, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    if tokens > 1:
+        lens[1] = max(width - 77, 1)  # a partial last chunk
+    if tokens > 2:
+        lens[2] = 0  # no active column
+    return dict(
+        q=fp8((tokens, H, D), 0.5, g),
+        swa_pool=swa_pool,
+        comp_pool=comp_pool,
+        indices=indices,
+        lens=lens,
+        sinks=torch.randn(H, device=DEVICE, generator=g),
+    )
+
+
+def reference(
+    c: dict, bmm1_scale: float, bmm2_scale: float, sinks: torch.Tensor | None
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """FP32 sparse attention over each token's active columns (K = V)."""
+    swa = c["swa_pool"].reshape(-1, D).float()
+    comp = c["comp_pool"].reshape(-1, D).float()
+    q = c["q"].float()
+    out = torch.zeros(q.shape, device=DEVICE)
+    for t in range(q.shape[0]):
+        n = int(c["lens"][t])
+        idx = c["indices"][t, :n].long()
+        cols = torch.arange(n, device=DEVICE)
+        keep = idx >= 0
+        if not bool(keep.any()):
+            continue
+        rows = torch.where(
+            (cols < SWA)[:, None],
+            swa[idx.clamp(0, swa.shape[0] - 1)],
+            comp[idx.clamp(0, comp.shape[0] - 1)],
+        )[keep]
+        s = (q[t] @ rows.T) * bmm1_scale
+        m = s.max(dim=1).values
+        if sinks is not None:
+            m = torch.maximum(m, sinks)
+        p = torch.exp(s - m[:, None])
+        denom = p.sum(dim=1)
+        if sinks is not None:
+            denom = denom + torch.exp(sinks - m)
+        out[t] = (p @ rows) / denom[:, None] * bmm2_scale
+    return out
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("width", [128, 200, 384, 512, 640])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [1, 6, 48])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_sinks", [True, False])
+def test_matches_reference(width: int, tokens: int, with_sinks: bool) -> None:
+    c = make_case(tokens, width, seed=width * 1000 + tokens)
+    # The kernel takes only tokens whose clusters are all resident at once,
+    # which depends on the device's SM count (read once the case's tensors
+    # have made the device's context current).
+    tokens = min(tokens, _max_tokens(c["q"].device.index, -(-width // 128)))
+    c.update({key: c[key][:tokens] for key in ("q", "indices", "lens")})
+    sinks = c["sinks"] if with_sinks else None
+    bmm1_scale, bmm2_scale = D**-0.5 * 1.25, 0.75
+    out = torch.full((tokens, H, D), float("nan"), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE)
+    args = (c["q"], c["swa_pool"], c["comp_pool"], c["indices"], c["lens"], out)
+    assert supports_sparse_mla_cute(*args, bmm1_scale, bmm2_scale, sinks)
+    sparse_mla_decode(*args, bmm1_scale, bmm2_scale, sinks)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    ref = reference(c, bmm1_scale, bmm2_scale, sinks)
+    got = out.float()
+    assert not torch.isnan(got).any()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got, ref, atol=0.03, rtol=0.05)
+    if tokens > 2:
+        assert bool((got[2] == 0).all())
+
+
+def test_cuda_graph_replay_matches_eager() -> None:
+    c = make_case(12, 640, seed=7)

+"""A TP all-gather over NVLink multicast with a Lamport mailbox, for the
+specialized decode.
+
+The specialized decode gathers small tensors across the TP group on its
+critical path: each dense indexer layer of a row-sharded decode step gathers
+its top-k rows (and the candidate source its candidate blocks), and every step
+gathers the vocab-parallel logits. A few hundred kilobytes at most, so the
+latency of the collective, not its bandwidth, is what counts.
+
+vLLM's custom all-gather has a Lamport kernel for NVLink multicast
+(``mnnvl_lamport_all_gather``), but it never waits for the rank's own
+multicast copy: it takes its own slot from registers, and a copy that lands
+after the next call has cleaned its stage stays there. A later gather of
+another size lays the slots out differently and can read that word as a
+peer's payload. A stress test of back-to-back gathers of alternating sizes in
+CUDA graphs hits this hundreds of times in a few million gathers. This module
+is a gather of the same shape that cannot leave a word behind.
+
+The mailbox is symmetric memory with a multicast mapping, laid out as
+16-byte packs::
+
+    mailbox[generation][rank][pack]    3 generations x TP ranks x capacity
+
+A call runs one kernel, one thread a 16-byte pack of the rank's input:
+
+1. Publish: the thread stores its pack through the multicast address into
+   every rank's ``mailbox[g][rank][pack]``. A word equal to the Lamport
+   sentinel (``0x80000000``: FP32 negative zero, INT32_MIN) goes out as 0.
+2. Collect: it polls ``mailbox[g][r][pack]`` of every rank ``r``, its own
+   included, until no word of it is the sentinel; writes each rank's pack to
+   the output, rank-major as NCCL lays out a dim-0 gather; and stores the
+   sentinel back into the slots it read. Every slot a call writes is read
+   after it has landed and reset by the same call, so no call leaves a word
+   for a later one, whatever the sizes.
+3. Generation: ``state[0]`` is the call's generation. Each CTA reads it once
+   and counts itself in ``state[1]``; the last CTA to arrive advances the
+   generation and clears the count. A rank can be at most one call ahead of
+   a peer (finishing a call needs every rank's payload), so a rank writing
+   the next generation never touches the slots a slower peer still reads;
+   three generations, as vLLM's and FlashInfer's Lamport kernels use, leave
+   one more in between.
+
+The kernel triggers its PDL dependents once it has published. The output
+holds the sanitized words on every rank, its own slot included, so all ranks
+see the same bits. The caller must issue calls in the same order on every
+rank and on one stream: calls on one instance must not overlap.

+        [address.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip)],

+        "=r,=r,=r,=r,l",

+                dtype=torch.int32,
+                device=device,
+            )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Decode top-k of the dense indexers straight from their BF16 logits, in CuTe DSL.
+
+The problem. In a decode step each dense indexer layer scores every compressed
+token of a row (SM100's paged MQA logits are BF16) and keeps the ``k`` largest:
+the token top-512, and in the candidate source also the top-2048 of the rows'
+8-token block maxima. ``cooperative_topk`` reads FP32, so the logits used to be
+upcast first, and it builds a radix histogram of every value with shared-memory
+atomics. Real indexer logits crowd a few histogram bins (a row of 150K logits
+holds about 200 distinct BF16 values), where those atomics serialize.
+
+What this module computes. ``DecodeTopK`` writes, for each row, the indices of
+its ``k`` largest elements in any order (exact: every index whose value exceeds
+the k-th largest, then enough of those equal to it), or ``0 .. n-1`` and -1
+padding when the row has at most ``k`` elements. An element is one BF16 logit
+(token mode), or the NaN-propagating maximum of an aligned group of 8 logits
+(block mode, the candidate blocks), with the row's newest block pinned at +inf
+and blocks scoring -inf written as -1. Values are compared through an
+order-preserving 16-bit key of their BF16 bits, so ties are exact.
+
+How. One thread block cluster of ``C`` CTAs per row: 8 CTAs of 512 threads
+while every row's cluster can be resident at once, else 4 of 1024 (a second
+wave of clusters would nearly double the time). Each CTA copies one
+contiguous chunk of the row into shared memory, as 16-byte vectors (8 logits,
+or one block); the chunks split the row's valid length, not its width. A
+thread stages 8 vectors and keeps them in registers too, so a cluster holds
+262,144 logits. Wider rows need more: at a 1M context the ratio-2 layers'
+logits are 524,288 wide, and a second build stages 16 vectors a thread at 8
+CTAs, the other 8 in shared memory only. The candidate source layer scores
+every token (ratio 1), 1,048,576 at a 1M context, so a third build runs 16
+CTAs a row (a non-portable cluster size, which CuTe DSL allows on every
+kernel) with 16 vectors a thread. Rows of the wide builds run in waves when
+they outnumber the resident clusters; the 16-CTA build takes at most two
+waves (`supports_decode_topk`). Two ways to the answer:
+
+- Sampled (token rows longer than one vector a thread)::
+
+      sample the row ──► every CTA: the same cutoff (the q-th largest of the
+      row's 2048 samples, q aiming at 3k survivors)
+         └► keep keys > cutoff and up to k keys == cutoff, push both to CTA 0
+              └► CTA 0: exact k-th largest among <= 8192 survivors (two 8-bit
+                 radix passes), write k indices
+
+- Direct (block mode, short token rows, and a sample that misjudged the row:
+  more than 8192 survivors, or fewer than k at or above the cutoff): the exact
+  k-th largest key from two cluster-wide 8-bit radix histograms, then every
+  CTA writes its own selected indices straight to the output.
+
+Both filter the same way: a thread tests each of its vectors' maximum against
+the cutoff, the vectors that can hold selected keys go to a CTA queue, and
+the CTA's threads unpack the queued vectors evenly; a CTA scan gives each
+thread its output slots and one cluster atomic reserves the CTA's range, so no
+key costs an atomic. Whole-row histograms spread each warp's atomics over 8
+copies (lane l counts into copy l mod 8), since a crowded bin serializes the
+atomics on its word; the radix selects over the few thousand samples or
+survivors count into one histogram, where the copies' zeroing and summing
+cost more than they save.
+
+Synchronization. Cluster barriers separate the phases: every CTA has started
+and zeroed its counters before any distributed shared memory access; samples
+are complete before the cutoff; survivors are complete before CTA 0 reads
+them; histogram contributions are complete before they are read; and CTA 0
+waits until every peer is done with its shared memory before it exits. The
+kernel waits on its predecessor grid before reading inputs and lets its
+dependents launch once its chunk is in shared memory (programmatic dependent
+launch).

+            [_v(Uint32(a), loc, ip), _v(Uint32(b), loc, ip)],
+            "max.NaN.bf16x2 $0, $1, $2;",
+            "=r,r,r",
+            False,
+            loc,
+            ip,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+@dsl_user_op
+def shfl_up(value: Uint32, delta: int, *, loc=None, ip=None) -> Uint32:
+    """``value`` of the lane ``delta`` below (own value in the lowest lanes)."""
+    return Uint32(
+        _asm(
+            T.i32(),
+            [_v(Uint32(value), loc, ip)],
+            f"shfl.sync.up.b32 $0, $1, {delta}, 0, 0xffffffff;",
+            "=r,r",
+            True,
+            loc,
+            ip,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+@dsl_user_op
+def shared_red(address: Int32, value: Uint32, *, loc=None, ip=None) -> None:
+    """Atomic add to a shared word of this CTA."""
+    _asm(
+        None,
+        [_v(Int32(address), loc, ip), _v(Uint32(value), loc, ip)],
+        "red.shared.add.u32 [$0], $1;",
+        "r,r",
+        True,
+        loc,
+        ip,
+    )

+@dsl_user_op
+def peer_address(address: Int32, rank, *, loc=None, ip=None) -> Int32:
+    """The cluster address of this CTA's shared ``address`` in CTA ``rank``."""
+    return Int32(
+        _asm(
+            T.i32(),
+            [_v(Int32(address), loc, ip), _v(Int32(rank), loc, ip)],
+            "mapa.shared::cluster.u32 $0, $1, $2;",
+            "=r,r,r",
+            False,
+            loc,
+            ip,

+    )

+@dsl_user_op
+def cluster_add_u64(address: Int32, value: Int64, *, loc=None, ip=None) -> Int64:
+    """Atomic add to an 8-byte aligned cluster shared word pair; returns the
+    old value."""

+        _asm(
+            T.i64(),
+            [_v(Int32(address), loc, ip), _v(Int64(value), loc, ip)],
+            "atom.shared::cluster.add.u64 $0, [$1], $2;",
+            "=l,r,l",
+            True,
+            loc,
+            ip,

+@dsl_user_op
+def cluster_red(address: Int32, value: Uint32, *, loc=None, ip=None) -> None:

+        None,
+        [_v(Int32(address), loc, ip), _v(Uint32(value), loc, ip)],

+@dsl_user_op
+def cluster_load(address: Int32, *, loc=None, ip=None) -> Uint32:
+    """Load a cluster shared word."""

+        _asm(
+            T.i32(),
+            [_v(Int32(address), loc, ip)],

+@dsl_user_op
+def cluster_store_u32(address: Int32, value, *, loc=None, ip=None) -> None:
+    """Store a 32-bit word to cluster shared memory."""

+        None,
+        [_v(Int32(address), loc, ip), _v(Uint32(value), loc, ip)],

+@dsl_user_op

+    """Store the low half of a word to cluster shared memory."""
+    _asm(
+        None,
+        [_v(Int32(address), loc, ip), _v(Uint32(value), loc, ip)],
+        "{\n.reg .b16 h;\ncvt.u16.u32 h, $1;\nst.shared::cluster.u16 [$0], h;\n}",

+@cute.jit
+def order_key(bits: Uint32) -> Uint32:
+    """The order-preserving key of the BF16 value in the low half of ``bits``:
+    a larger value has a larger key, NaNs of either sign outside the
+    numbers."""
+    b = bits & Uint32(0xFFFF)
+    return b ^ (Uint32(0x8000) | ((Uint32(0) - (b >> Uint32(15))) & Uint32(0x7FFF)))
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def block_key(w0: Uint32, w1: Uint32, w2: Uint32, w3: Uint32) -> Uint32:
+    """The key of the NaN-propagating maximum of eight BF16 values."""
+    m = max_nan_bf16x2(max_nan_bf16x2(w0, w1), max_nan_bf16x2(w2, w3))
+    m = max_nan_bf16x2(m, (m >> Uint32(16)) | (m << Uint32(16)))
+    return order_key(m)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def hist_add(
+    hist_address: Int32, bin_: Uint32, valid, copies: bool, lane: Int32
+) -> None:
+    """Count each valid lane's ``bin_`` with one shared atomic. ``copies``:
+    lane ``l`` counts into copy ``l % COPIES`` of a ``[COPIES][256]``
+    histogram (whole-row histograms: crowded bins would serialize the
+    atomics of one copy); else into a plain 256-word one."""
+    if valid:
+        slot = Int32(bin_)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(copies):
+            slot = slot + (lane & (COPIES - 1)) * 256
+        shared_red(hist_address + slot * 4, Uint32(1))
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def select_bin(hist: cute.Tensor, q: Uint32, ctl: cute.Tensor, lane: Int32) -> None:
+    """Warp 0: the bin ``b`` of a 256-bin histogram holding the ``q``-th
+    largest entry (q >= 1), into ``ctl[BIN]``, and ``q`` minus the entries
+    in the bins above ``b`` into ``ctl[REMAIN]``. Lane ``l`` scans bins
+    ``255 - 8 l`` down to ``248 - 8 l``."""
+    low = shared_load_u32x4(Int32(hist.iterator.toint()) + (248 - 8 * lane) * 4)
+    high = shared_load_u32x4(Int32(hist.iterator.toint()) + (252 - 8 * lane) * 4)
+    counts = (high[3], high[2], high[1], high[0], low[3], low[2], low[1], low[0])
+    local = Uint32(0)
+    for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(8):
+        local = local + counts[i]
+    inclusive = local
+    for shift in cutlass.range_constexpr(5):
+        below = shfl_up(inclusive, 1 << shift)
+        if lane >= (1 << shift):
+            inclusive = inclusive + below
+    above = inclusive - local
+    if (above < q) & (inclusive >= q):
+        found = Int32(-1)
+        remain = Uint32(0)
+        for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(8):
+            if (found < 0) & (above + counts[i] >= q):
+                found = Int32(255 - 8 * lane - i)
+                remain = q - above
+            above = above + counts[i]
+        ctl[BIN] = Uint32(found)
+        ctl[REMAIN] = remain
+

+class DecodeTopK:
+    """The decode top-k (module docstring) of rows of BF16 logits.
+
+    ``k``: 512, 1024 or 2048; ``cluster``: 4, 8 or 16 CTAs a row (4: 1024
+    threads, else 512); ``vector_count``: 16-byte vectors a thread stages (8,
+    or 16 at 8 or 16 CTAs: the first 8 also stay in registers), so a row
+    holds at most ``cluster * threads * vector_count`` vectors;
+    ``block_mode``: elements are 8-logit block maxima.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, k: int, cluster: int, vector_count: int, block_mode: bool
+    ) -> None:
+        assert k in TOP_KS and cluster in (4, 8, 16)
+        assert vector_count in vector_choices(cluster)
+        self.k = k
+        self.cluster = cluster
+        self.threads = threads_for(cluster)
+        self.warps = self.threads // 32
+        self.block_mode = block_mode
+        self.per_vector = 1 if block_mode else 8  # elements a 16-byte vector holds
+        self.vector_count = vector_count
+        self.vectors = self.threads * vector_count  # a CTA's vectors
+        self.samples = SAMPLES // cluster  # a CTA's samples, one a thread
+        assert self.samples <= self.threads
+        self.max_elements = cluster * self.vectors * self.per_vector
+        # Token rows of at most one vector a thread take the direct path.
+        self.direct_elements = cluster * self.threads * self.per_vector
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        logits_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+        lengths_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+        out_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+        rows: Int32,
+        row_bytes: Int64,
+        width: Int32,
+        out_stride: Int32,
+        fallback: Int32,
+        stream: cuda.CUstream,
+    ):
+        """``logits``: BF16 rows ``row_bytes`` apart (16-byte aligned), each
+        valid below ``lengths[r]`` (int32, clamped to [0, width]); ``out``:
+        int32 rows ``out_stride`` apart. ``fallback`` nonzero forces the
+        direct path (tests)."""
+        self.kernel(
+            cute.make_tensor(lengths_ptr, cute.make_layout(rows)),
+            cute.make_tensor(out_ptr, cute.make_layout(rows * out_stride)),
+            logits_ptr.toint(),
+            row_bytes,
+            width,
+            out_stride,
+            fallback,
+        ).launch(
+            grid=(rows * self.cluster, 1, 1),
+            block=[self.threads, 1, 1],
+            cluster=[self.cluster, 1, 1],
+            stream=stream,
+            use_pdl=True,
+        )
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def vector_words(self, data_address: Int32, vector: Int32):
+        """The four words of the chunk's vector ``vector`` in shared memory."""
+        return shared_load_u32x4(data_address + vector * 16)
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def vector_top(self, words, element: Int32, pinned: Int32) -> Uint32:
+        """The largest key of a staged vector whose first element is
+        ``element`` (block mode: the pinned newest block ranks first)."""
+        top = block_key(words[0], words[1], words[2], words[3])
+        if cutlass.const_expr(self.block_mode):  # noqa: SIM102
+            if element == pinned:
+                top = Uint32(POS_INF_KEY)
+        return top
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def word_key(self, words, e: int, element: Int32, pinned: Int32) -> Uint32:
+        """The key of element ``e`` of a vector's ``words`` (``element``: its
+        row index, for the pinned block)."""
+        key = Uint32(0)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(self.block_mode):
+            key = block_key(words[0], words[1], words[2], words[3])
+            if element == pinned:
+                key = Uint32(POS_INF_KEY)
+        else:
+            key = order_key(Uint32(words[e // 2]) >> Uint32(16 * (e % 2)))
+        return key
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def scan2(self, a: Uint32, b: Uint32, scan: cute.Tensor, tid: Int32):
+        """Exclusive CTA prefix sums of ``a`` and ``b`` over the threads, and
+        their totals (every thread calls it; three barriers)."""
+        lane = tid & 31
+        warp = tid >> 5
+        in_a = a
+        in_b = b
+        for shift in cutlass.range_constexpr(5):
+            below_a = shfl_up(in_a, 1 << shift)
+            below_b = shfl_up(in_b, 1 << shift)
+            if lane >= (1 << shift):
+                in_a = in_a + below_a
+                in_b = in_b + below_b
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()  # the previous scan's readers are done
+        if lane == 31:
+            scan[warp] = in_a
+            scan[32 + warp] = in_b
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+        if warp == 0:
+            sum_a = Uint32(0)
+            sum_b = Uint32(0)
+            if lane < self.warps:
+                sum_a = Uint32(scan[lane])
+                sum_b = Uint32(scan[32 + lane])
+            run_a = sum_a
+            run_b = sum_b
+            for shift in cutlass.range_constexpr(5):
+                below_a = shfl_up(run_a, 1 << shift)
+                below_b = shfl_up(run_b, 1 << shift)
+                if lane >= (1 << shift):
+                    run_a = run_a + below_a
+                    run_b = run_b + below_b
+            scan[64 + lane] = run_a - sum_a
+            scan[96 + lane] = run_b - sum_b
+            if lane == 31:
+                scan[128] = run_a
+                scan[129] = run_b
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+        first_a = Uint32(scan[64 + warp]) + in_a - a
+        first_b = Uint32(scan[96 + warp]) + in_b - b
+        return first_a, first_b, Uint32(scan[128]), Uint32(scan[129])
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def radix_select(
+        self,
+        keys: cute.Tensor,
+        count: Int32,
+        q: Uint32,
+        hist: cute.Tensor,
+        hist2: cute.Tensor,
+        ctl: cute.Tensor,
+        tid: Int32,
+    ):
+        """The ``q``-th largest of ``keys[0:count]`` (shared Uint16, q <= count)
+        and how many of the keys equal to it rank within the top ``q``. Every
+        thread calls it."""
+        lane = tid & 31
+        h1 = Int32(hist.iterator.toint())
+        h2 = Int32(hist2.iterator.toint())
+        if tid < 256:
+            hist[tid] = Uint32(0)
+            hist2[tid] = Uint32(0)
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+        iterations = (count + self.threads - 1) // self.threads
+        for it in cutlass.range(iterations, unroll=4):
+            i = it * self.threads + tid
+            valid = i < count
+            key = Uint32(0)
+            if valid:
+                key = Uint32(keys[i])
+            hist_add(h1, key >> Uint32(8), valid, False, lane)
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+        if tid < 32:
+            select_bin(hist, q, ctl, lane)
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+        high = Uint32(ctl[BIN])
+        remain = Uint32(ctl[REMAIN])
+        for it in cutlass.range(iterations, unroll=4):
+            i = it * self.threads + tid
+            key = Uint32(0)
+            if i < count:
+                key = Uint32(keys[i])
+            hist_add(
+                h2,
+                key & Uint32(0xFF),
+                (i < count) & ((key >> Uint32(8)) == high),
+                False,
+                lane,
+            )
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+        if tid < 32:
+            select_bin(hist2, remain, ctl, lane)
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+        tau = (high << Uint32(8)) | Uint32(ctl[BIN])
+        need = Uint32(ctl[REMAIN])
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+        return tau, need
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def queue_vectors(
+        self,
+        regs,
+        data_address: Int32,
+        cutoff: Uint32,
+        start: Int32,
+        length: Int32,
+        pinned: Int32,
+        tid: Int32,
+        scan,
+        queue,
+    ) -> Int32:
+        """Queue this CTA's vectors that can hold a key >= ``cutoff`` (by
+        their maximum) and return how many (every thread)."""
+        threads, per = self.threads, self.per_vector
+        hits = Uint32(0)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(VECTORS):
+            first = (j * threads + tid) * per
+            if first < length:
+                words = (regs[j, 0], regs[j, 1], regs[j, 2], regs[j, 3])
+                if self.vector_top(words, start + first, pinned) >= cutoff:
+                    hits = hits | Uint32(1 << j)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(self.vector_count > VECTORS):  # noqa: SIM102
+            # Only a chunk reaching the shared-only vectors visits them.
+            if VECTORS * threads * per < length:
+                for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(VECTORS, self.vector_count):
+                    first = (j * threads + tid) * per
+                    if first < length:
+                        words = self.vector_words(data_address, j * threads + tid)
+                        if self.vector_top(words, start + first, pinned) >= cutoff:
+                            hits = hits | Uint32(1 << j)
+        slot, _, total, _ = self.scan2(
+            Uint32(cute.arch.popc(hits)), Uint32(0), scan, tid
+        )
+        position = Int32(slot)
+        if hits != Uint32(0):
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(self.vector_count):
+                if (hits >> Uint32(j)) & Uint32(1) != Uint32(0):
+                    queue[position] = Uint16(j * threads + tid)
+                    position = position + 1
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+        return Int32(total)
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def count_queued(
+        self,
+        data_address: Int32,
+        queued: Int32,
+        cutoff: Uint32,
+        start: Int32,
+        length: Int32,
+        pinned: Int32,
+        tid: Int32,
+        queue,
+    ):
+        """This thread's keys above and equal to ``cutoff`` in its share of
+        the queued vectors (entries ``tid``, ``tid + threads``, ...)."""
+        per = self.per_vector
+        gt = Uint32(0)
+        eq = Uint32(0)
+        for q in cutlass.range(tid, queued, self.threads, unroll=1):
+            vector = Int32(queue[q])
+            words = self.vector_words(data_address, vector)
+            for e in cutlass.range_constexpr(per):
+                element = vector * per + e
+                key = self.word_key(words, e, start + element, pinned)
+                if element < length:
+                    if key > cutoff:
+                        gt = gt + Uint32(1)
+                    if key == cutoff:
+                        eq = eq + Uint32(1)
+        return gt, eq
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def reserve(self, gt: Uint32, eq: Uint32, totals: int, tid: Int32, ctl, scan):
+        """This thread's first slots for its ``gt`` / ``eq`` keys in the
+        cluster-wide lists counted at CTA 0's ``ctl[totals]`` pair: a CTA
+        scan, then one 64-bit cluster atomic for the CTA."""
+        first_gt, first_eq, cta_gt, cta_eq = self.scan2(gt, eq, scan, tid)
+        if tid == 0:
+            old = cluster_add_u64(
+                peer_address(Int32(ctl.iterator.toint()) + totals * 4, 0),
+                Int64(cta_gt) | (Int64(cta_eq) << Int64(32)),
+            )
+            ctl[BASE_GT] = Uint32(old & Int64(0xFFFFFFFF))
+            ctl[BASE_EQ] = Uint32(old >> Int64(32))
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+        return Int32(Uint32(ctl[BASE_GT]) + first_gt), Int32(
+            Uint32(ctl[BASE_EQ]) + first_eq
+        )
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def gather(
+        self,
+        regs,
+        data_address: Int32,
+        cutoff: Uint32,
+        start: Int32,
+        length: Int32,
+        pinned: Int32,
+        tid: Int32,
+        ctl,
+        scan,
+        queue,
+        g_key,
+        g_idx,
+        g_eq,
+    ):
+        """Sampled path: push this CTA's keys above ``cutoff`` and up to k
+        equal to it to CTA 0 and return the cluster's totals (every CTA)."""
+        k, per = self.k, self.per_vector
+        queued = self.queue_vectors(
+            regs, data_address, cutoff, start, length, pinned, tid, scan, queue
+        )
+        gt, eq = self.count_queued(
+            data_address, queued, cutoff, start, length, pinned, tid, queue
+        )
+        slot_gt, slot_eq = self.reserve(gt, eq, TOTALS, tid, ctl, scan)
+        key_remote = peer_address(Int32(g_key.iterator.toint()), 0)
+        idx_remote = peer_address(Int32(g_idx.iterator.toint()), 0)
+        eq_remote = peer_address(Int32(g_eq.iterator.toint()), 0)
+        for q in cutlass.range(tid, queued, self.threads, unroll=1):
+            vector = Int32(queue[q])
+            words = self.vector_words(data_address, vector)
+            for e in cutlass.range_constexpr(per):
+                element = vector * per + e
+                key = self.word_key(words, e, start + element, pinned)
+                if element < length:
+                    if key > cutoff:
+                        if slot_gt < CAPACITY:
+                            cluster_store_u16(key_remote + slot_gt * 2, key)
+                            cluster_store_u32(
+                                idx_remote + slot_gt * 4, Uint32(start + element)
+                            )
+                        slot_gt = slot_gt + 1
+                    if key == cutoff:
+                        if slot_eq < k:
+                            cluster_store_u32(
+                                eq_remote + slot_eq * 4, Uint32(start + element)
+                            )
+                        slot_eq = slot_eq + 1
+        cute.arch.cluster_arrive()
+        cute.arch.cluster_wait()
+        totals = peer_address(Int32(ctl.iterator.toint()) + TOTALS * 4, 0)
+        return cluster_load(totals), cluster_load(totals + 4)
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def count_vector(
+        self,
+        level: int,
+        words,
+        first: Int32,
+        start: Int32,
+        length: Int32,
+        pinned: Int32,
+        high: Uint32,
+        hist_address: Int32,
+        lane: Int32,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Count a staged vector (``words``, its first element ``first``) into
+        a whole-row histogram: level 0 the high bytes of its keys, level 1
+        the low bytes of those whose high byte is ``high``."""
+        per = self.per_vector
+        if cutlass.const_expr(level == 0):
+            if cute.arch.vote_any_sync(first < length):
+                for e in cutlass.range_constexpr(per):
+                    key = self.word_key(words, e, start + first + e, pinned)
+                    hist_add(
+                        hist_address, key >> Uint32(8), first + e < length, True, lane
+                    )
+        else:
+            # Only vectors reaching the selected high byte count.
+            top = self.vector_top(words, start + first, pinned)
+            reach = (first < length) & ((top >> Uint32(8)) >= high)
+            if cute.arch.vote_any_sync(reach):
+                for e in cutlass.range_constexpr(per):
+                    key = self.word_key(words, e, start + first + e, pinned)
+                    hist_add(
+                        hist_address,
+                        key & Uint32(0xFF),
+                        reach & (first + e < length) & ((key >> Uint32(8)) == high),
+                        True,
+                        lane,
+                    )
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def exact_cutoff(
+        self,
+        regs,
+        data_address: Int32,
+        start: Int32,
+        length: Int32,
+        pinned: Int32,
+        tid: Int32,
+        ctl,
+        hist,
+        hist_a,
+        hist_b,
+    ):
+        """The row's exact k-th largest key and how many keys equal to it
+        rank within the top k, from every CTA's vectors: two cluster-wide
+        radix histograms gathered at CTA 0 (every CTA)."""
+        threads, per = self.threads, self.per_vector
+        lane = tid & 31
+        hist_address = Int32(hist.iterator.toint())
+        high = Uint32(0)
+        remain = Uint32(self.k)
+        for level in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+            target = hist_a if level == 0 else hist_b
+            for i in cutlass.range(tid, 256 * COPIES, threads, unroll=1):
+                hist[i] = Uint32(0)
+            cute.arch.sync_threads()
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(VECTORS):
+                self.count_vector(

+"""The sparse-MLA decode of small batches, in CuTe DSL.
+
+The problem. In a decode step every query token (DeepSeek-V4's MLA after the
+query projection: 16 heads a rank at TP4, FP8 E4M3, head dim 512) attends to
+its own sparse set of KV rows. A row is 512 FP8 bytes and serves as both K and
+V. The set holds up to 640 columns: the 128 sliding-window rows of one KV pool,
+then the indexer's top-k rows of the compressed pool, all addressed as storage
+offsets into their pool, with -1 for an unused column and a per-token count of
+active columns. TRTLLM-gen splits a token's 640 rows over at most 3 CTAs, so at
+one or two requests (6 or 12 tokens with DSpark) its kernel runs about 10 µs
+on a GPU of 152 SMs; most of that is the latency of one CTA's serial work.
+
+What this module computes. ``sparse_mla_decode`` writes, for each token ``t``
+and head ``h``, the BF16 attention output over the token's active columns ``c``
+(``c < lens[t]`` and ``indices[t, c] >= 0``)::
+
+    s_c = bmm1_scale * q[t, h] . kv[c]
+    p_c = exp(s_c - m)
+    out[t, h] = bmm2_scale * sum_c p_c kv[c] / (sum_c p_c + exp(sink_h - m))
+
+where ``kv[c]`` is row ``indices[t, c]`` of the sliding-window pool for the
+first 128 columns and of the compressed pool for the others, ``m`` is the
+maximum of the scores and the sink, and the sink term is omitted without sinks.
+A token with no active column gets zeros. This is what
+``trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4`` computes for these shapes.
+
+How. One CTA of 128 threads takes one token and one 128-column chunk of its
+sparse set (chunk 0 = the sliding-window columns); the ``n = ceil(width / 128)``
+chunks of a token form a thread block cluster, so a 640-wide layer runs 5 CTAs
+a token in parallel::
+
+    gather the chunk's KV rows and the query (cp.async, one group per 128-byte K
+    block) into 128B-swizzled tiles
+      └► S^T = KV x Q^T on tcgen05 (M 128 rows, N 16 heads, K 512, FP8 -> FP32 TMEM)
+           └► chunk softmax per head in base 2: max m_c, sum l_c, and
+              P^T = 256 * exp2(S - m_c) as FP8 (scaled: small weights stay normal)
+                └► O^T = V^T x P^T on tcgen05, V the same tile read MN-major
+                   (four MMAs of 128 head dims) ...
+                └► ... while the cluster exchanges (m_c, l_c) per head (st.async)
+                     └► each CTA scales its partial O by exp2(m_c - M) / L
+                        (M, L over the cluster's chunks and the sink)
+                          └► block j of the 512 head dims goes to CTA j % n, which
+                             sums the n partials and stores BF16
+
+The partial blocks travel by bulk copies between the CTAs' shared memory into
+the receiving CTA's KV tile, whose MMAs are done by then: a cluster barrier
+after each CTA's second MMA separates the two uses. A last cluster barrier keeps
+every CTA resident until the bulk copies reading its shared memory are complete.
+
+Synchronization. The kernel reads the sinks (weights) before its grid
+dependency wait and everything else after it, and lets its dependents launch
+once its S MMAs are issued (programmatic dependent launch). Masked columns
+gather zeros and score -inf.
+
+Scope. Two CTAs fit an SM (about 78 KB of shared memory each), so a launch is
+one wave only while every token's cluster can be resident: ``_max_tokens`` allows
+2 x the device's resident clusters of ``n`` CTAs at one CTA an SM (on a 152-SM
