+def bf16_arguments(experts, routed: nn.Module) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """The per-layer arguments of the BF16 experts op, read from the stock
+    TrtLlmBf16ExpertsMonolithic and its RoutedExperts as the stock layer passes them
+    (RoutedExperts.forward_monolithic -> apply_monolithic -> apply, with the
+    post-expert-norm hook attached, so do_finalize=False)."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.trtllm_bf16_moe import (
+        view_as_block_major_k,
+    )
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.utils import fi_moe_largest_bucket
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils import (
+        activation_to_flashinfer_int,
+    )
+
+    if experts.post_gemm2_hook is None:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "The stock BF16 experts finalize inside the op, so the experts op "
+            "would differ from the stock one."
+        )
+    if routed.routing_sink is not None:
+        raise RuntimeError("Routed experts capture is not supported.")
+    if experts.topk != TOP_K:
+        raise RuntimeError("Unexpected stock BF16 experts configuration.")
+    return dict(
+        routing_bias=routed.e_score_correction_bias,
+        gemm1_weights=view_as_block_major_k(routed.w13_weight),
+        gemm2_weights=view_as_block_major_k(routed.w2_weight),
+        num_experts=routed.global_num_experts,
+        top_k=experts.topk,
+        n_group=routed.num_expert_group,
+        topk_group=routed.topk_group,
+        intermediate_size=experts.intermediate_size_per_partition,
+        local_expert_offset=experts.ep_rank * experts.local_num_experts,
+        local_num_experts=experts.local_num_experts,
+        routed_scaling_factor=routed.routed_scaling_factor,
+        routing_method_type=experts.routing_method_type,
+        activation_type=activation_to_flashinfer_int(routed.activation),
+        tune_max_num_tokens=fi_moe_largest_bucket(experts.moe_config),
+        routing_replay_out=None,
+        do_finalize=False,
+    )
+
+
+def stock_experts(moe: nn.Module) -> tuple[Any, nn.Module]:
+    """The stock experts kernel and RoutedExperts of a MuseSpark1xMoE."""
+    routed = moe.experts.routed_experts
+    kernel = getattr(routed.quant_method, "moe_kernel", None)
+    if kernel is None:
+        raise RuntimeError("The stock MoE layer has no experts kernel.")
+    return kernel.fused_experts, routed
+
+
+def stock_all_reduce(communicator) -> tuple[Any, str | None]:
+    """The TP communicator's FlashInfer all-reduce wrapper, checked to take the
+    decode's [PREPARED_MAX, HIDDEN] bf16 rows (so the stock layers' all-reduce
+    is this one), and the backend its workspace resolved to
+    (VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND; auto: MNNVL, on one node TRT-LLM where
+    MNNVL has no multicast). Creates the workspace on first use, collectively
+    over the TP group, as the stock path does; vLLM keeps one per process, so
+    every caller reads the same backend."""
+    from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.flashinfer_all_reduce import (
+        get_fi_ar_workspace,
+    )
+
+    wrapper = getattr(communicator, "fi_ar_comm", None)
+    if wrapper is None or wrapper.disabled:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "The specialized decode's all-reduce needs vLLM's FlashInfer all-reduce."
+        )
+    probe = torch.empty(
+        (PREPARED_MAX, HIDDEN), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=communicator.device
+    )
+    if not wrapper.should_use_fi_ar(probe):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"vLLM's FlashInfer all-reduce does not take [{PREPARED_MAX}, {HIDDEN}] "
+            "bf16 here."
+        )
+    workspace = get_fi_ar_workspace(
+        world_size=wrapper.world_size,
+        rank=wrapper.rank,
+        max_token_num=wrapper.max_num_tokens,
+        hidden_dim=HIDDEN,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        group=wrapper.group,
+    )
+    return wrapper, getattr(workspace, "backend", None)
+
+
+def stock_sum_order(communicator) -> str:
+    """The sum order of the stock TP all-reduce (``stock_all_reduce``'s backend,
+    ``BACKEND_SUM_ORDERS``), the one the fused all-reduces over the TP group
+    take. Raises for a backend whose order they do not reproduce. Collective
+    over the TP group on the process's first call."""
+    _, backend = stock_all_reduce(communicator)
+    order = BACKEND_SUM_ORDERS.get(backend) if backend is not None else None
+    if order is None:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"The fused all-reduce has no sum order for vLLM's {backend!r} "
+            "FlashInfer all-reduce."
+        )
+    return order
+
+
+def bind_all_reduce(communicator):
+    """The TP communicator's FlashInfer all-reduce wrapper, checked to be the MNNVL
+    all-reduce the stock layers take for [PREPARED_MAX, HIDDEN] bf16
+    (``stock_all_reduce``)."""
+    backend = envs.VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND
+    if backend not in ALL_REDUCE_BACKENDS:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"The TP8/16 all-reduce needs the MNNVL backend, got {backend!r}."
+        )
+    wrapper, resolved = stock_all_reduce(communicator)
+    if resolved != "mnnvl":
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "vLLM's FlashInfer all-reduce did not resolve to the MNNVL backend."
+        )
+    return wrapper
+
+
+def tp_coordinator(group):
+    """The TP GroupCoordinator, given it or its device group."""
+    tp = get_tp_group()
+    if group is not tp and group is not tp.device_group:
+        raise ValueError("FlashInferOps.build takes the TP group.")
+    return tp
+
+
+def _finite(rows: torch.Tensor) -> str:
+    """How finite ``rows`` are, and their largest finite magnitude."""
+    finite = torch.isfinite(rows)
+    largest = rows.float().abs().masked_fill(~finite, 0).max() if rows.numel() else 0
+    return f"{int(finite.sum())}/{rows.numel()} finite (max |x| {float(largest):.3g})"
+
+
+# The expert-TP build probe: rel L2 of a layer's TP route rows, summed across
+# ranks, against its EP rows (expected ~3e-3: one more BF16 rounding per rank;
+# a wrong slice or scale gives O(1)).
+EXPERT_TP_PROBE_MAX = 1e-2
+
+
+class FlashInferOps:
+    """``RoutedExpertsOps``: the routed experts of every MoE layer and the TP16
+    all-reduce.
+
+    build() binds every per-layer argument and checks every requirement once, then
+    runs each op once at b = 8 (rank-symmetric; the all-reduce workspace is created
+    lazily otherwise). The calls are graph-capturable and read no per-step state.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.nvfp4: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
+        self.bf16: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
+        self.all_reduce_wrapper = None
+        # The NVFP4 calls below the public op (prepare_from_metadata).
+        self.nvfp4_calls: dict[int, Nvfp4Call] = {}
+        self.prepared: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
+        self.body_workspace: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...] = ()
+        # Per token count, the (tile, config) keys of the tactics the NVFP4
+        # op takes (prepare_from_metadata).
+        self.valid_tactics: dict[int, set[tuple[int, int]]] = {}
+        # Expert TP: the NVFP4 layers on TP experts (their arguments in
+        # nvfp4), the TP experts' bytes and each layer's build probe.
+        self.tp_experts: set[int] = set()
+        self.tp_bytes = 0
+        self.probe_rel_l2: dict[int, float] = {}
+        # Their tactic (pin_tp_tactic) and the preferences it came from; None:
+        # the op's untuned default.
+        self.tp_preferred: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...] = ()
+        self.tp_tactic: tuple[int, int] | None = None
+
+    def build(
+        self, group, layers: tuple[nn.Module, ...], use_expert_tp: bool = False
+    ) -> None:
+        """``layers``: the stock decoder layers (layer_idx, feed_forward).
+
+        With ``use_expert_tp`` (collective over the TP group, which must equal the
+        stock layers' EP group), every NVFP4 layer runs on TP experts resharded
+        from the stock ones (finalized by the package's TP tail); BF16 layers
+        stay EP (stock weights, the EP tail)."""
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.trtllm_bf16_moe import (
+            TrtLlmBf16ExpertsMonolithic,
+        )
+        from vllm.models.muse_spark.nvidia.muse_moe_runner import (
+            MuseSparkTrtLlmNvFp4Experts,
+        )
+
+        tp = tp_coordinator(group)
+        for layer in layers:
+            experts, routed = stock_experts(layer.feed_forward)
+            if isinstance(experts, MuseSparkTrtLlmNvFp4Experts):
+                self.nvfp4[layer.layer_idx] = nvfp4_arguments(experts, routed)
+            elif isinstance(experts, TrtLlmBf16ExpertsMonolithic):
+                self.bf16[layer.layer_idx] = bf16_arguments(experts, routed)
+            else:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"Layer {layer.layer_idx} runs {type(experts).__name__}, not "
+                    "the TRT-LLM-gen experts the specialized decode calls."
+                )
+        seconds = 0.0
+        if use_expert_tp:
+            # Before the calls below the op are prepared: they bind the
+            # arguments, one shape for every NVFP4 layer.
+            start = time.perf_counter()
+            self.shard_experts(tp, layers)
+            seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
+        self.prepare_from_metadata()
+        if use_expert_tp:
+            # After the calls are prepared: the tactic needs a prepared body.
+            self.pin_tp_tactic(tp)
+        self.warm_up()
+        if use_expert_tp:
+            self.log_expert_tp(tp.world_size, seconds)
+        if tp.world_size in MNNVL_TPS:
+            # At TP8 only the check: the attention boundary sums in this
+            # all-reduce's order.
+            communicator = tp.device_communicator
+            wrapper = bind_all_reduce(communicator)
+            if tp.world_size in ALL_REDUCE_TPS:
+                self.all_reduce_wrapper = wrapper
+                x = torch.zeros(
+                    (BATCHES[0], HIDDEN),
+                    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                    device=communicator.device,
+                )
+                self.all_reduce(x)
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------- expert TP
+    def shard_experts(self, tp, layers: tuple[nn.Module, ...]) -> None:
+        """Replaces every NVFP4 layer's arguments by its TP experts': reshard
+        (collective) and a probe against the stock EP op. Collective over
+        ``tp``: the placement check is agreed across the ranks before any
+        rank raises, so none is left waiting in the reshard."""
+        if not self.nvfp4:
+            raise RuntimeError("Expert TP needs NVFP4 layers.")
+        group = tp.device_group
+        nvfp4_layers = [layer for layer in layers if layer.layer_idx in self.nvfp4]
+        ep_ranks = {
+            stock_experts(layer.feed_forward)[0].ep_rank for layer in nvfp4_layers
+        }
+        wrong = sorted(ep_ranks - {tp.rank_in_group})
+        reason = (
+            f"got EP rank {wrong[0]} on TP rank {tp.rank_in_group}" if wrong else None
+        )
+        reason = expert_tp.agree(tp.cpu_group, reason, "cpu")
+        if reason is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Expert TP needs the EP rank to be the TP rank: {reason}."
+            )
+        for layer in nvfp4_layers:
+            index = layer.layer_idx
+            experts, routed = stock_experts(layer.feed_forward)
+            ep_args = self.nvfp4[index]
+            shards = expert_tp.reshard_nvfp4(
+                stock_shards(ep_args, experts), group, routed.global_num_experts
+            )
+            tp_args = tp_arguments(ep_args, shards)
+            self.probe_rel_l2[index] = self.probe(
+                index, tp_args, group, experts.quant_config.a1_gscale
+            )
+            self.nvfp4[index] = tp_args
+            self.tp_experts.add(index)
+            self.tp_bytes += sum(
+                t.numel() * t.element_size()
+                for t in shards
+                if isinstance(t, torch.Tensor)
+            )
+
+    def log_expert_tp(self, tp: int, seconds: float) -> None:
+        """Logs the expert-TP build: what was resharded, its memory, the build
+        probes and the tactic the decode batch takes (None: no body prepared
+        for it, so the public op runs)."""
+        args = self.nvfp4[min(self.tp_experts)]
+        num_local = args["local_num_experts"]
+        tactic = tactic_key(self.tp_tactic or -1, BATCHES[0], num_local)
+        probes = self.probe_rel_l2.values()
+        pinned = (
+            "the op's default: no preferred tactic valid on every rank"
+            if self.tp_tactic is None
+            else f"pinned: preference {self.tp_preferred.index(self.tp_tactic) + 1}"
+            f" of {len(self.tp_preferred)}, on every rank"
+        )
+        logger.info(
+            "Muse Spark expert TP built: TP%d, %d NVFP4 layers (%d BF16 layers "
+            "EP), %d experts at intermediate %d per rank, +%.2f GiB per rank, "
+            "probe rel L2 %.3g..%.3g, tactic %s at %d tokens (%s), %.1f s",
+            tp,
+            len(self.tp_experts),
+            len(self.bf16),
+            num_local,
+            args["intermediate_size"],
+            self.tp_bytes / 2**30,
+            min(probes),
+            max(probes),
+            tactic if tactic in self.prepared else None,
+            BATCHES[0],
+            pinned,
+            seconds,
+        )
+
+    def probe_inputs(
+        self, device: torch.device, global_scale: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> tuple[ExpertsInput, RoutedTopk]:
+        """The build probe's input at the decode batch, the same on every rank
+        (seeded): unit-RMS rows quantized with ``global_scale`` (the layer's
+        NVFP4 input global scale), so they stay in the range the layer's scales
+        were calibrated for, and routes spread over all experts, so every EP
+        rank serves some."""
+        from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
+
+        b = BATCHES[0]
+        g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(20261023)
+        x = torch.randn((b, POOLED), generator=g, device=device)
+        a, a_sf = ops.scaled_fp4_quant(
+            x.to(torch.bfloat16), global_scale, is_sf_swizzled_layout=False
+        )
+        inputs = ExpertsInput(a, a_sf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).reshape(b, -1))
+        routes = torch.arange(b * TOP_K, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        stride = NUM_EXPERTS // (b * TOP_K)
+        topk = RoutedTopk(
+            (routes * stride + routes // TOP_K % stride).view(b, TOP_K),
+            torch.full((b, TOP_K), 1.0 / TOP_K, device=device),
+        )
+        return inputs, topk
+
+    def probe(
+        self,
+        layer: int,
+        tp_args: dict[str, Any],
+        group,
+        global_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> float:
+        """Rel L2 of the layer's TP route rows, summed across ranks, against its
+        stock EP rows on the same stock-quantized input (collective); raises
+        above EXPERT_TP_PROBE_MAX on every rank."""
+        inputs, topk = self.probe_inputs(tp_args["gemm1_weights"].device, global_scale)
+        outputs = []
+        for args in (self.nvfp4[layer], tp_args):
+            out = self.public_routed_experts(args, inputs, topk)
+            outputs.append((out.gemm2_permuted, out.expanded_idx_to_permuted_idx))
+        rel = expert_tp.probe_rel_l2(outputs[0], outputs[1], group)
+        if not rel < EXPERT_TP_PROBE_MAX:
+            ep_rows, ep_local = expert_tp.route_rows(*outputs[0])
+            tp_rows, _ = expert_tp.route_rows(*outputs[1])
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Layer {layer}: the TP experts differ from the stock EP experts "
+                f"by rel L2 {rel:.3g} (at most {EXPERT_TP_PROBE_MAX}); on this "
+                f"rank the EP rows of its {int(ep_local.sum())} routes are "
+                f"{_finite(ep_rows[ep_local])}, its TP partial rows "
+                f"{_finite(tp_rows)}."
+            )
+        logger.debug("Muse Spark expert TP: layer %d probe rel L2 %.3g", layer, rel)
+        return rel
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def expert_tp_tactics() -> tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]:
+        """The preferred expert-TP tactics measured on the installed FlashInfer's
+        batched-GEMM cubin package; none for any other package."""
+        from flashinfer.artifacts import ArtifactPath
+
+        return EXPERT_TP_TACTICS.get(ArtifactPath.TRTLLM_GEN_BMM, ())
+
+    def pin_tp_tactic(self, tp) -> None:
+        """The TP experts' tactic: the first of expert_tp_tactics() that the op
+        takes for 1 to ROUTING_MAX_TOKENS tokens and that has a prepared body,
+        on every rank of the TP group, else the op's untuned default.
+        Collective over ``tp``'s CPU group (every rank runs the same FlashInfer
+        build, so the same list); nothing is timed, so the same weights and
+        FlashInfer build take the same tactic at every start."""
+        self.tp_preferred = self.expert_tp_tactics()
+        self.tp_tactic = None
+        if not self.tp_preferred:
+            from flashinfer.artifacts import ArtifactPath
+
+            logger.warning(
+                "Muse Spark expert TP: no tactics measured for FlashInfer's "
+                "batched-GEMM cubins %s; the TP experts run the op's untuned "
+                "default tactic.",
+                ArtifactPath.TRTLLM_GEN_BMM,
+            )
+            return
+        usable = torch.tensor(
+            [
+                int(
+                    tactic in self.prepared
+                    and all(tactic in valid for valid in self.valid_tactics.values())
+                )
+                for tactic in self.tp_preferred
+            ],
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+        )
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(
+            usable, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MIN, group=tp.cpu_group
+        )
+        first = next((i for i, ok in enumerate(usable.tolist()) if ok), None)
+        if first is None:
+            logger.warning(
+                "Muse Spark expert TP: none of the tactics %s is valid on every "
+                "rank; the TP experts run the op's untuned default tactic.",
+                self.tp_preferred,
+            )
+            return
+        self.tp_tactic = self.tp_preferred[first]
+
+    def public_routed_experts(
+        self, args: dict[str, Any], inputs: ExpertsInput, topk: RoutedTopk
+    ) -> UnfinalizedMoEOutput:
+        """The public routed op on ``args``."""
+        import flashinfer
+
+        num_tokens = inputs.a.shape[0]
+        output = flashinfer.fused_moe.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(
+            topk_ids=(topk.ids, topk.weights),
+            hidden_states=inputs.a,
+            hidden_states_scale=inputs.a_sf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).reshape(
+                num_tokens, -1
+            ),
+            **args,
+        )

+"""The Muse Spark DSpark draft's fused Markov sampling loop.
+
+``DSparkSpeculator`` samples the draft tokens left to right, adding each
+step's Markov bias to the base draft logits. ``MarkovSampler`` runs that loop
+with each step's tail as one CuTe DSL kernel (``cutedsl/draft/markov.py``),
+bitwise equal to the speculator's eager loop on rows without NaN.
+
+Each row samples the lowest vocab id whose noised logit is NaN, else the
+lowest id of the maximum (the ``torch.argmax`` order), at every block size and
+vocab shard. On a row with a NaN the eager loop's pick depends on its block
+layout, so the two can differ there.
+
+With a vocab-parallel Markov w2 each rank samples its own vocab range
+(``VocabParallelMarkovHead``) and the ranks exchange one packet per request
+and step. The draft model builds it on the first call of its
+``sample_sequential`` hook, from the speculator's sampling state.
+"""
+
+import dataclasses
+import functools
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any, NamedTuple
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm.distributed import (
+    get_tensor_model_parallel_rank,
+    get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size,
+)
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import QuantizationConfig
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.utils import dispatch_unquantized_gemm
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import (
+    ParallelLMHead,
+    UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.models.qwen3_dspark import DSparkMarkovHead
+from vllm.model_executor.models.utils import maybe_prefix
+from vllm.models.common.ops.sequence_parallel import sp_all_gather
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv, round_up
+
+from ..cutedsl.common.policy import batch_table
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# gumbel_sample's BLOCK_SIZE.
+MARKOV_BLOCK = 1024
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class FusedMarkovParams:
+    """Static inputs of the fused loop, fixed once the draft model loads."""
+
+    w1: torch.Tensor
+    """Markov w1 table ``[V, R]`` (bf16, R a power of two)."""
+    vocab_size: int
+    output_multiplier: float
+    """Rounded to fp32, as torch multiplies an fp32 tensor by it."""
+    soft_cap: float | None
+    """Rounded to fp32; ``None`` without a soft cap."""
+    inv_soft_cap: float
+    """``fp32(1) / fp32(soft_cap)``: torch divides by a scalar this way."""
+    vocab_shard: "MarkovVocabShard | None" = None
+    """Set when ``markov_w2`` is vocab-parallel."""
+

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class MarkovVocabShard:
+    """This rank's contiguous vocab range of the draft lm_head and Markov w2."""
+
+    tp_size: int
+    size: int
+    offset: int
+

+# Rows up to which markov_step launches with programmatic dependent launch,
+# so that its blocks start while the w2 GEMV runs. Measured on GB300, the
+# overlap pays at one and two rows and costs from three rows on.
+STEP_PDL_MAX_ROWS = 2
+
+# markov_step's vocab entries per CTA, by row count; other row counts take
+# MARKOV_BLOCK. Smaller blocks spread a step over more SMs; on GB300 at the
+# TP8 vocab shard 512 beat MARKOV_BLOCK at most row counts up to 16. Every row
+# samples the same id at any block size: each argmax takes the first NaN, else
+# the first maximum.
+STEP_BLOCKS = batch_table("0-16:512")
+MIN_STEP_BLOCK = min(MARKOV_BLOCK, *STEP_BLOCKS.values())

+def step_block(num_rows: int) -> int:
+    """markov_step's block for a call over ``num_rows`` rows."""
+    return STEP_BLOCKS.get(num_rows, MARKOV_BLOCK)

+class VocabParallelMarkovHead(DSparkMarkovHead):
+    """``DSparkMarkovHead`` with ``markov_w2`` sharded like the draft lm_head:
+    each rank computes its vocab range of the transition bias
+    (``local_bias``)."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        vocab_size: int,
+        draft_vocab_size: int,
+        markov_rank: int,
+        prefix: str,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        # DSparkMarkovHead.__init__ would first allocate the replicated w2:
+        # the same modules are built here, with the w2 sharded from the start.
+        nn.Module.__init__(self)
+        self.markov_w1 = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, markov_rank)
+        # The same parameter name and loader as the replicated w2, sharded.
+        self.markov_w2 = ParallelLMHead(
+            draft_vocab_size,
+            markov_rank,
+            bias=False,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "markov_w2"),
+        )
+        self.markov_w2._retain_weight_for_gather = False
+        self.markov_w2.is_w4a16_nvfp4 = False
+        # Rank-local w2 rows padded to a 16-byte row count, set by
+        # align_vocab_shard() once the weights are loaded.
+        self._local_w2: torch.Tensor | None = None
+
+    def align_vocab_shard(self) -> None:
+        """Back the rank's unquantized ``markov_w2`` rows with storage padded
+        by zero rows to a 16-byte multiple, read by :meth:`local_bias`.
+
+        cuBLAS picks its GEMV kernel by shape; the padded shard keeps the
+        replicated head's sums, an unaligned one does not.
+        """
+        if not isinstance(self.markov_w2.quant_method, UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod):
+            return
+        weight = self.markov_w2.weight
+        if (
+            self._local_w2 is not None
+            and weight.data_ptr() == self._local_w2.data_ptr()
+        ):
+            # A reload wrote into the padded storage, which captured CUDA
+            # graphs keep reading.
+            return
+        rows = weight.shape[0]
+        per_16_bytes = 16 // weight.element_size()
+        padded = weight.new_zeros((round_up(rows, per_16_bytes), weight.shape[1]))
+        padded[:rows].copy_(weight)
+        weight.data = padded[:rows]
+        self._local_w2 = padded
+
+    def local_bias(self, markov_embed: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """This rank's vocab shard of the transition bias ([B, r] -> [B, V/tp]).
+
+        The result is a view with the row stride of the padded storage.
+        """
+        assert self._local_w2 is not None
+        rows = self.markov_w2.weight.shape[0]
+        return dispatch_unquantized_gemm()(
+            self.markov_w2, markov_embed, self._local_w2
+        )[:, :rows]
+
+
+def markov_vocab_shard(model: Any) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+    """This rank's ``[start, end)`` draft-vocab range of a vocab-parallel
+    Markov w2, or None when the w2 is replicated.
+
+    Called once the weights are loaded; prepares the padded w2 storage

+    computations would not return this range's columns of
+    ``model.compute_draft_logits`` and ``model.markov_bias`` on the default
+    GEMM (under ``--linear-backend`` they match to rounding only).

+            "The vocab-parallel Markov head needs an unquantized bf16 Markov w2"
+        )

+    w2_range = w2.shard_indices

+        # the logits processor and UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod.apply unless
+        # --linear-backend selects another one.
+        model.logits_processor.scale != 1.0

+        or w2.num_embeddings_padded != vocab_size
+        or lm_head.num_embeddings_padded != vocab_size
+        or w2_range.added_vocab_end_index != w2_range.added_vocab_start_index
+        or lm_range.added_vocab_end_index != lm_range.added_vocab_start_index
+        or (w2_range.org_vocab_start_index, w2_range.org_vocab_end_index)
+        != (lm_range.org_vocab_start_index, lm_range.org_vocab_end_index)
+    ):

+            "The vocab-parallel Markov head needs a logits processor without "
+            "scale or soft cap, no VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT, and a draft lm_head "
+            "and Markov w2 split into the same unpadded vocab ranges"

+def compute_local_draft_logits(model: Any, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """This rank's vocab shard of ``model.compute_draft_logits``, ungathered."""
+    return model.logits_processor(
+        model.lm_head, hidden_states.to(model.lm_head.weight.dtype), skip_gather=True

+def vocab_shard(params: FusedMarkovParams, start: int, end: int) -> MarkovVocabShard:
+    """The sharded loop's view of this rank's draft-vocab range.

+    The packets and cache shards are gathered in TP rank order, so rank k
+    must hold the k-th equal slice of the draft vocabulary. The w2 is
+    never replicated in this mode, so a draft the loop does not take fails
+    at its first draft step instead of running the eager loop on gathered
+    shards.
+    """
+    tp_size = get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
+    size = end - start
+    if tp_size & (tp_size - 1):
+        reason = f"a power-of-two TP size, not {tp_size}"
+    elif size * tp_size != params.vocab_size:
+        reason = (
+            f"a draft vocabulary ({params.vocab_size}) that TP {tp_size} "
+            "divides without padding"
+        )
+    elif start != size * get_tensor_model_parallel_rank():
+        reason = "TP rank k to hold the k-th slice of the draft vocabulary"
+    else:

+    raise ValueError(f"The vocab-parallel Markov head needs {reason}")

+    d2t = getattr(model, "draft_id_to_target_id", None)

+        return "the platform is not CUDA"
+    if getattr(model, "output_logit_transform_params", None) is None:
+        return "the draft has no output-logit transform"
+    if draft_topk is not None:
+        return "dspark_draft_topk is set"
+    if watermarked:

+    if use_fp64_gumbel:

+def fused_markov_params(model: Any, draft_logits: torch.Tensor) -> FusedMarkovParams:

+    eager loop does through the bf16 d2t scatter buffer, and it applies the

+        vocab_size=draft_logits.shape[-1],
+        output_multiplier=float(fp32(multiplier)),
+        soft_cap=None if cap is None else float(cap),
+        inv_soft_cap=1.0 if cap is None else float(fp32(1.0) / cap),

+
+def build_markov_sampler(
+    model: Any,
+    *,
+    draft_logits: torch.Tensor | None,
+    draft_topk: int | None,
+    watermarked: bool,
+    use_fp64_gumbel: bool,
+    sample_from_anchor: bool,
+    max_num_reqs: int,
+    num_steps: int,

+    runs: a draft it does not reproduce fails at its first draft step, as the
+    vocab-parallel Markov w2 has no eager loop."""
+    reason = unsupported(
+        model,
+        draft_logits=draft_logits,
+        draft_topk=draft_topk,
+        watermarked=watermarked,
+        use_fp64_gumbel=use_fp64_gumbel,
+        sample_from_anchor=sample_from_anchor,
+    )
+    if reason is not None:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "The Muse Spark specialized decode runs the fused DSpark Markov "
+            f"loop, which does not run here: {reason}"
+        )

+    params = fused_markov_params(model, draft_logits)

+    if local_range is not None:
+        shard = vocab_shard(params, *local_range)

+            "Using the vocab-parallel DSpark Markov sampling loop.",
+            scope="process",

+
+class MarkovCall(NamedTuple):
+    """The views one call of the fused loop runs on (``MarkovSampler.call_views``)."""
+
+    width: int
+    """Vocab entries per rank: the whole vocab, or this rank's shard."""
+    offset: int

+    base_logits: torch.Tensor
+    """``[rows, n_spec, width]`` BF16."""
+    markov_bias: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor]
+    cache: torch.Tensor

+    flat_cache: torch.Tensor | None
+    """With a shard, the flat cache the all-gather moves (else None)."""
+    packets: torch.Tensor
+    """``[rows, 4]`` FP32: a row's packet (with a shard)."""
+    idx_map: torch.Tensor
+    pos: torch.Tensor
+    markov_embeds: torch.Tensor
+    """``[n_spec + 1, rows, rank]``."""

+    num_blocks: int

+    step_pdl: bool

+
+class MarkovSampler:
+    """The fused Markov loop of one draft model, with its per-call buffers."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        model: Any,
+        params: FusedMarkovParams,
+        max_num_reqs: int,
+        num_steps: int,

+        self._pdl = current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()

+        # takes views of their leading elements.
+        rows, n_spec, w1 = max_num_reqs, num_steps, params.w1
+        shard = params.vocab_shard
+        width = params.vocab_size if shard is None else shard.size

+        def empty(numel: int, dtype: torch.dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
+            return torch.empty(numel, dtype=dtype, device=w1.device)
+

+        self._markov_block_argmax = empty(rows * num_blocks, torch.int64)
+        self._markov_block_max = empty(rows * num_blocks, torch.float32)
+        # Blocks of each row that finished their step, zeroed per call.
+        self._markov_arrivals = empty(rows, torch.int32)

+        # draft-logits shard the custom all-gather moves in 16-byte vectors.
+        sharded = shard is not None

+        self._markov_cache = empty(
+            round_up(rows * n_spec * width, 8) if sharded else 0, torch.bfloat16
+        )

+        self._kernels = kernels
+        self._loop: Any = None
+        if not w1.is_cuda:
+            return

+        # step at every (block, PDL, vector) a call over 1 to max_num_reqs
+        # rows takes.

+            w1,
+            self._markov_embeds,
+            width=width,
+            has_cap=params.soft_cap is not None,
+            tp=None if shard is None else shard.tp_size,
+            steps=self._step_variants(rows, width, draft_logits),
+            pick_pdl=self._pdl,
+            fill_vector=kernels.fill_vectorized(

+                # stride the padded flat shard (a multiple of 8 elements).

+                src_s0=round_up(n_spec * width, 8),
+                cache=kernels.Operand.of(draft_logits),
+                shard=width,

+    def _heads(self) -> tuple[Callable, Callable]:
+        """``(base logits, Markov bias)`` of a call: the draft's full-vocab
+        heads, or with a vocab shard this rank's (neither all-gathers)."""
+        if self.params.vocab_shard is None:

+        return (
+            functools.partial(compute_local_draft_logits, self.model),
+            self.model.model.markov_head.local_bias,
+        )
+
+    def _step_variants(
+        self, max_rows: int, width: int, draft_logits: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> set[tuple[int, bool, bool]]:
+        """The ``(block, PDL, vector)`` of every step a call over 1 to
+        ``max_rows`` rows launches (``MarkovKernels.step`` picks ``vector``
+        from its operands).
+
+        The base logits and the bias of a call are fresh outputs of the
+        heads (``_heads``): their row strides are the heads' own (a padded
+        lm_head or Markov w2 leaves its padded rows' stride under the
+        ``[..., :vocab]`` view the logits processor returns), read here from
+        one call of each on zeros, and they start as aligned as these
+        probes do (allocator blocks)."""
+        kernels, n_spec, w1 = self._kernels, self.num_steps, self.params.w1
+        base_head, bias_head = self._heads()
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            base_probe = base_head(w1.new_zeros(2, self.model.config.hidden_size))
+            bias_probe = bias_head(w1.new_zeros(2, w1.shape[1]))
+        base_row = base_probe.stride(0)
+        bias = kernels.Operand(bias_probe.data_ptr(), (bias_probe.stride(0), 1))
+        if self.params.vocab_shard is not None:
+            cache = kernels.Operand(
+                self._markov_cache.data_ptr(), (n_spec * width, width, 1)
+            )
+        else:
+            cache = kernels.Operand.of(draft_logits)
+        variants = set()
+        for rows in range(1, max_rows + 1):
+            block = step_block(rows)
+            pdl = self._pdl and rows <= STEP_PDL_MAX_ROWS
+            for col in range(n_spec):
+                vector = kernels.vectorized(
+                    block,
+                    width=width,
+                    col=col,
+                    # Column col of the [rows, n_spec, width] view.
+                    base=kernels.Operand(
+                        base_probe.data_ptr() + col * base_row * 2,
+                        (n_spec * base_row, 1),
+                    ),
+                    bias=bias,
+                    cache=cache,
+                )
+                variants.add((block, pdl, vector))

+
+    def call_views(
+        self,
+        num_reqs: int,
+        head_hidden: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        sample_indices: torch.Tensor,
+        sample_idx_mapping: torch.Tensor,
+        sample_pos: torch.Tensor,
+        draft_logits: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> MarkovCall:
+        """The base logits of a call over ``num_reqs`` rows and the views of

+        n_spec = self.num_steps
+        num_sample = num_reqs * n_spec
+        shard = self.params.vocab_shard
+        rank = self.params.w1.shape[1]

+        base_logits = base_head(head_hidden[sample_indices[:num_sample]])
+        flat_cache = None
+        if shard is None:
+            width, offset = self.params.vocab_size, 0
+            cache = draft_logits
+        else:
+            width, offset = shard.size, shard.offset
+            # The custom all-gather moves 16-byte vectors: pad the flat shard.
+            numel = num_sample * width
+            flat_cache = self._markov_cache[: round_up(numel, 8)]
+            cache = flat_cache[:numel].view(num_reqs, n_spec, width)

+        num_blocks = cdiv(width, block)

+            width=width,
+            offset=offset,
+            base_logits=base_logits.view(num_reqs, n_spec, width),
+            markov_bias=markov_bias,
+            cache=cache,
+            flat_cache=flat_cache,
+            packets=self._markov_packets[: num_reqs * 4].view(num_reqs, 4),
+            idx_map=sample_idx_mapping[:num_sample].view(num_reqs, n_spec),
+            pos=sample_pos[:num_sample].view(num_reqs, n_spec),
+            # Row i holds the Markov embedding that step i reads.
+            markov_embeds=self._markov_embeds[: (n_spec + 1) * num_reqs * rank].view(

+            arrivals=self._markov_arrivals[:num_reqs],
+            block=block,
+            num_blocks=num_blocks,
+            block_argmax=self._markov_block_argmax[: num_reqs * num_blocks],
+            block_max=self._markov_block_max[: num_reqs * num_blocks],
+            step_pdl=self._pdl and num_reqs <= STEP_PDL_MAX_ROWS,
+        )
+        for tensor, dtype in (
+            (call.base_logits, torch.bfloat16),
+            (call.cache, torch.bfloat16),
+            (call.idx_map, torch.int64),
+            (call.pos, torch.int64),
+        ):
+            assert tensor.dtype == dtype, (tensor.dtype, dtype)
+        return call
+
+    def sample(
+        self,
+        num_reqs: int,
+        head_hidden: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        sample_indices: torch.Tensor,
+        sample_idx_mapping: torch.Tensor,
+        sample_pos: torch.Tensor,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        anchor_idx: torch.Tensor,

+        draft_logits: torch.Tensor,

+        """The eager Markov loop with each step's tail as one kernel.

+        Writes ``draft_tokens`` and the ``draft_logits`` cache for the first
+        ``num_reqs`` requests, as ``DSparkSpeculator``'s eager loop does over
+        the same buffers. (The specialized decode refuses adaptive
+        verification, so there is no confidence head to run.)
+
+        With a vocab shard each rank samples its own vocab range, the ranks
+        exchange one packet per request and step, and one all-gather after the
+        loop fills the full-vocab draft-logits cache.
+        """
+        params = self.params
+        call = self.call_views(
+            num_reqs,
+            head_hidden,
+            sample_indices=sample_indices,
+            sample_idx_mapping=sample_idx_mapping,
+            sample_pos=sample_pos,
+            draft_logits=draft_logits,
+        )
+        for tensor, dtype in (
+            (seeds, torch.int64),
+            (temperature, torch.float32),
+            (draft_tokens, torch.int64),

+                draft_logits,
+                sample_idx_mapping,
+                num_reqs,
+                self.num_steps,
+                call.width,

+        self.eps = attn.rms_norm_eps
+        self.num_kv_heads = attn.num_kv_heads
+        self.oproj, self.qkv, self.out, self.partial = oproj, qkv, out, partial
+
+    @classmethod
+    def unsupported(cls, vllm_config) -> str | None:
+        from . import cute_ops
+
+        if not cute_ops.qkv_front_available():
+            return cute_ops.unavailable(cute_ops.QKV_FRONT_KERNEL)
+        if not cute_ops.attn2_available():
+            return cute_ops.unavailable(cute_ops.ATTN2_KERNEL)
+        return None
+
+    @classmethod
+    def build(cls, ctx: BuildContext, layer: nn.Module | None) -> "QkvAttention":
+        from ..cutedsl.oproj.batt import OProjection
+        from . import cute_ops
+
+        assert layer is not None
+        attn = layer.self_attn
+        reason = cute_ops.unsupported_attn2(attn) or cute_ops.unsupported_projection(
+            attn
+        )
+        if reason is None and (
+            attn.use_attn_temperature_tuning or not attn.fused_qk_norm_rope_kv_insert
+        ):
+            reason = "attention without the stock fused QK-norm/RoPE/KV insert"
+        if reason is not None:
+            raise ValueError(f"layer {layer.layer_idx}: {reason}")
+        n = attn.qkv_proj.weight.shape[0]
+        cute_ops.prepare_qkv_front(n, BATCHES)
+        qkv = _scratch(ctx, "qkv", (PREPARED_MAX, n), torch.bfloat16)
+        out = _scratch(
+            ctx,
+            "attention",
+            (PREPARED_MAX, attn.num_heads * attn.head_dim),
+            torch.bfloat16,
+        )
+        partial = _scratch(ctx, "partial", (PREPARED_MAX, HIDDEN), torch.bfloat16)
+        # attn2 splits a long context over a fixed number of clusters (the
+        # deployment's, so the captured launch fits every step); the split
+        # merge's workspace is shared by the layers, which run in order, sized
+        # for the full-attention layers' splits (a window only lowers them)
+        # and zeroed once (every launch leaves its counters zero).
+        window = cute_ops.attn2_window(attn.attn.sliding_window, ctx.max_context)
+        num_splits = cute_ops.attn2_splits(ctx.max_context, window, attn.num_kv_heads)
+        cute_ops.prepare_attn2(ctx.max_context, window, attn.num_kv_heads, num_splits)
+        workspace = None
+        if cute_ops.attn2_split_kernel(ctx.max_context, window):
+            size = cute_ops.attn2_workspace_bytes(
+                PREPARED_MAX // cute_ops.QUERY_LEN,
+                attn.num_kv_heads,
+                cute_ops.attn2_splits(ctx.max_context, 0, attn.num_kv_heads),
+            )
+            workspace = ctx.buffers.get("attn2_workspace")
+            if workspace is None:
+                workspace = torch.zeros(size, dtype=torch.uint8, device=ctx.device)
+                ctx.buffers["attn2_workspace"] = workspace
+            assert workspace.shape == (size,), "attn2_workspace"
+        return cls(
+            attn,
+            OProjection.build(ctx, layer),
+            qkv,
+            out,
+            partial,
+            ctx.max_context,
+            window,
+            num_splits,
+            workspace,
+        )
+
+    def prepare_kv(self) -> None:
+        from . import cute_ops
+
+        kv_cache = self.attn.attn.kv_cache
+        if not isinstance(kv_cache, torch.Tensor) or kv_cache.numel() == 0:
+            return
+        if not cute_ops.kv_cache_layout_ok(kv_cache, self.num_kv_heads):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{self.layer_name}: KV cache {tuple(kv_cache.shape)} "
+                f"{kv_cache.stride()} {kv_cache.dtype} is not the 16-byte aligned "
+                f"bf16 [pages, {self.num_kv_heads}, 16, 128] layout with dense "
+                "pages the decode kernels read"
+            )
+
+    def front_call(
+        self, step: Step, x: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None:
+        """(kv_cache, slot_mapping) of this layer's QKV front call on ``x``
+        (the step's attention input) into its qkv rows in the current forward
+        context, or None if the kernel does not take the call. Host state
+        only: shapes, dtypes, strides and alignment, the same on every rank
+        (prepare_kv holds every rank's KV cache to the aligned layout)."""
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention.attention import (
+            get_attention_context,
+        )
+
+        from . import cute_ops
+
+        _, _, kv_cache, slot_mapping = get_attention_context(self.layer_name)
+        if slot_mapping is None or not cute_ops.supports_call(
+            x,
+            self.weight,
+            step.positions,
+            self.cos_sin_cache,
+            slot_mapping,
+            kv_cache,
+            self.num_kv_heads,
+            self.qkv[: x.shape[0]],
+        ):
+            return None
+        return kv_cache, slot_mapping
+
+    def run(self, step: Step, metadata: Any, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        from . import cute_ops
+
+        b = x.shape[0]
+        # plan() leaves a step the front does not take to the stock forward;
+        # front_call is the launch's check.
+        call = self.front_call(step, x)
+        if call is None:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"{self.layer_name}: the QKV front cannot take this step"
+            )
+        kv_cache, slot_mapping = call
+        qkv = self.qkv[:b]
+        cute_ops.launch_qkv_front(
+            x,
+            self.weight,
+            step.positions,
+            self.cos_sin_cache,
+            slot_mapping,
+            kv_cache,
+            qkv,
+            self.eps,
+        )
+        q, gate = cute_ops.split_qkv(qkv, self.num_kv_heads)
+        decode = metadata.decode
+        out = self.out[:b]
+        cute_ops.attn2(
+            q,
+            kv_cache,
+            decode.block_tables,
+            decode.seq_lens,
+            gate,
+            out,
+            self.num_kv_heads,
+            max_seq_len=self.max_context,
+            window=self.window,
+            num_splits=self.num_splits,
+            workspace=self.workspace,
+        )
+        return self.oproj.run(out, self.partial[:b])
+
+
+def router_tier(router: nn.Module) -> str | None:
+    """Why the stock GateLinear would not run a vLLM-native kernel for the decode
+    batch (its last tier is F.linear, which follows --linear-backend), or None."""
+    native = (
+        "allow_ll_bf16_gemm",
+        "allow_fp32_router_gemm",
+        "allow_ll_fp32w_gemm",
+        "allow_bf16x3_router_gemm",
+    )
+    if not any(getattr(router, name, False) for name in native):
+        return "a router GEMM outside vLLM's native GateLinear tiers"
+    return None
+
+
+class RoutedMoE:
+    """The MoE: the stock router (GateLinear, asserted on a vLLM-native tier), the
+    routing short tail (``RoutedTopk``; the BF16 edge layers route inside the
+    experts op), the pooler (``ExpertsInput`` or ``ExpertsInputBf16``), the routed
+    experts (``RoutedExpertsOps`` -> ``UnfinalizedExperts``), the tail and the
+    unpooler GEMM, which publishes this rank's column block zero-copy into the
+    next boundary's mailbox.
+
+    With the short tail, the router and the routing run on an aux stream while the
+    pooler runs on the current one, joined before the routed experts. The fork and
+    join are issued directly, not through ``maybe_execute_in_parallel``, which runs
+    both sides in series under this model's breakable CUDA graph capture. The BF16
+    edge layers stay in series: their router logits feed the experts op on the
+    current stream."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        index: int,
+        moe: nn.Module,
+        ops: Any,
+        pooler: Any,
+        pooler_index: int,
+        tail: Any,
+        unpooler: Any,
+        routing: Any,
+        buffers: dict[str, torch.Tensor],
+        aux_stream: torch.cuda.Stream,
+    ):
+        self.index, self.moe, self.ops = index, moe, ops
+        self.pooler, self.pooler_index = pooler, pooler_index
+        self.tail, self.unpooler, self.routing = tail, unpooler, routing
+        self.ids, self.weights = buffers["topk_ids"], buffers["topk_weights"]
+        self.moe_out, self.columns = buffers["moe_out"], buffers["columns"]
+        self.aux_stream = aux_stream
+        self.forked, self.routed = torch.cuda.Event(), torch.cuda.Event()
+
+    @classmethod
+    def unsupported(cls, vllm_config) -> str | None:
+        from . import cute_ops
+
+        types = getattr(vllm_config.model_config.hf_text_config, "mlp_layer_types", ())
+        if any(kind != "sparse" for kind in types):
+            return "dense MLP layers"
+        if not cute_ops.routing_available():
+            return cute_ops.unavailable(cute_ops.ROUTING_KERNEL)
+        return None
+
+    @classmethod
+    def build(
+        cls,
+        ctx: BuildContext,
+        layer: nn.Module,
+        *,
+        ops: Any,
+        pooler: Any,
+        pooler_index: int,
+        tail: Any,
+        mailbox: Any,
+    ) -> "RoutedMoE":
+        """``mailbox``: the LamportMailbox of the boundary after this layer."""
+        from vllm.utils.torch_utils import aux_stream
+
+        from ..cutedsl.gemm.unpooler import Unpooler
+        from .cute_ops import MuseRouting
+
+        moe = layer.feed_forward
+        if moe.use_mega_moe or moe.pooler is None or moe.unpooler is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"layer {layer.layer_idx}: unsupported MoE form")
+        reason = router_tier(moe.router)
+        if reason is not None:
+            raise ValueError(f"layer {layer.layer_idx}: {reason}")
+        # The stock layer feeds the router the bf16 MoE input at decode batches
+        # (an fp32 copy only above 32 tokens); the router here reads the same.
+        if any(moe.wants_fp32_router_input(b) for b in BATCHES):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"layer {layer.layer_idx}: an fp32 router input at the decode batch"
+            )
+        routing = None if ops.is_bf16(layer.layer_idx) else MuseRouting(moe.moe_router)
+        buffers = {
+            "topk_ids": _scratch(ctx, "topk_ids", (PREPARED_MAX, TOP_K), torch.int32),
+            "topk_weights": _scratch(
+                ctx, "topk_weights", (PREPARED_MAX, TOP_K), torch.float32
+            ),
+            "moe_out": _scratch(ctx, "moe_out", (PREPARED_MAX, POOLED), torch.bfloat16),
+            "columns": _scratch(
+                ctx, "columns", (PREPARED_MAX, HIDDEN // ctx.tp), torch.bfloat16
+            ),
+        }
+        unpooler = Unpooler.from_moe(moe, ctx.tp, ctx.rank, mailbox=mailbox)
+        tail_layer = tail.bind(moe.post_expert_norm)
+        # The router's kernel for the decode batch, before capture.
+        moe.router(
+            torch.zeros(BATCHES[0], HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=ctx.device)
+        )
+        provider = cls(
+            layer.layer_idx,
+            moe,
+            ops,
+            pooler,
+            pooler_index,
+            tail_layer,
+            unpooler,
+            routing,
+            buffers,
+            aux_stream(),
+        )
+        provider.warm_up()
+        return provider
+
+    def warm_up(self) -> None:
+        """One eager pass, before capture, of the NVFP4 experts path a captured
+        step runs: the plan, the routing, the experts and the tail, so that
+        every first launch and first-use compile happens before capture. The
+        routes spread over all experts, so every EP rank runs its GEMMs.
+        Collective (the tail): every rank warms the same layers in the same
+        order."""
+        if self.routing is None:
+            return
+        b = BATCHES[0]
+        device = self.ids.device
+        inputs = ExpertsInput(
+            torch.zeros((b, POOLED // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device),
+            torch.zeros((b, POOLED // 16), device=device).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+        )
+        topk = RoutedTopk(self.ids[:b], self.weights[:b])
+        plan = self.ops.nvfp4_plan(self.index, inputs, topk)
+        # Sigmoid scores of 1 for b * TOP_K experts evenly apart, 0 elsewhere.
+        stride = NUM_EXPERTS // (b * TOP_K)
+        chosen = torch.arange(b * TOP_K, device=device).view(b, TOP_K) * stride
+        logits = torch.full((b, NUM_EXPERTS), -30.0, device=device)
+        logits.scatter_(1, chosen, 30.0)
+        self.routing(
+            logits, topk.ids, topk.weights, None if plan is None else plan.metadata
+        )
+        experts = self.ops.routed_experts(self.index, inputs, topk, plan)
+        self.tail.run(experts, self.moe_out[:b])
+
+    def prepare_kv(self) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def logits(self, x: torch.Tensor):
+        logits = self.moe.router(x)
+        return logits[0] if isinstance(logits, tuple) else logits
+
+    def run(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        b = x.shape[0]
+        if self.routing is None:
+            logits = self.logits(x)
+            rows = self.pooler.run(self.pooler_index, x)
+            experts = self.ops.routed_experts_bf16(self.index, rows, logits)
+        else:
+            self.forked.record()
+            a, a_sf = self.pooler.run(self.pooler_index, x)
+            inputs = ExpertsInput(a, a_sf)
+            topk = RoutedTopk(self.ids[:b], self.weights[:b])
+            # With a plan the routing also writes the experts' routing metadata,
+            # and the experts op runs without a routing kernel of its own.
+            plan = self.ops.nvfp4_plan(self.index, inputs, topk)
+            with torch.cuda.stream(self.aux_stream):
+                self.forked.wait()
+                self.routing(
+                    self.logits(x),
+                    topk.ids,
+                    topk.weights,
+                    None if plan is None else plan.metadata,
+                )
+                self.routed.record()
+            self.routed.wait()
+            experts = self.ops.routed_experts(self.index, inputs, topk, plan)
+        moe_out = self.moe_out[:b]
+        self.tail.run(experts, moe_out)
+        self.unpooler.run(moe_out, self.columns[:b])

+          MC_WORKERS_PER_CTX: "4"
+          VLLM_MOONCAKE_LOAD_RECV_THREADS: "4"
+          UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE: "n"
+          UCX_MEMTYPE_REG_WHOLE: "n"
+        json_args:
+          "--speculative-config": { num_speculative_tokens: 4, attention_backend: "KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA" }
+          "--compilation-config": { cudagraph_capture_sizes: [1, 7, 18, 34, 53, 64, 75, 100, 128, 150, 180, 200, 220, 240, 256, 280, 300, 320, 340, 360, 380, 400, 420, 440, 460, 480, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192] }
+    runbook: |
+      The B200 AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`kimik3-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic-dspark`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4759](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4759), pinned to [`9fe1038`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/tree/9fe10389c5e7866e7359cfd9620c9f27b2ccabf4/inferencex-e2e/benchmarks/multi_node/srt-slurm-recipes/kimik3/vllm/b200-fp4/agentx)) serves the default `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` checkpoint (MXFP4 weights) as one aggregated engine over two 8-GPU B200 nodes: TP8 within a node, PP2 across them, DCP8, vLLM's own frontend and the Inferact DSpark draft. It is a benchmark configuration; the settings in this preset are its production-useful parts. Throughput runs pin DSpark acceptance to InferenceX's golden acceptance lengths (3.84 at K7, 3.36 at K4), a benchmark control that is not part of the serving commands.
+
+      **Per-point settings.** `--max-num-seqs` is set per point and the CUDA graph sizes cover the decode batch sizes it needs, then the powers of two to 8192. The draft length falls with concurrency, and the target and draft attention backend change at concurrency 10:
+
+      | Concurrency | K | `--max-num-seqs` | Attention backend (target / draft) | Mooncake store |
+      | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+      | 1 | 7 | 2 | `TOKENSPEED_MLA` / `TOKENSPEED_MLA` | 200GB segment |
+      | 4 | 7 | 8 | `TOKENSPEED_MLA` / `TOKENSPEED_MLA` | 200GB segment |
+      | 10 | 7 | 16 | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` / `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | 200GB segment |
+      | 16 | 7 | 16 | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` / `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | off |
+      | 24 | 4 | 48 | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` / `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | off |
+      | 32 | 4 | 48 | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` / `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | off |
+      | 48 | 4 | 96 | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` / `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | 195GB segment |
+      | 96 | 4 | 192 | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` / `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | 195GB segment |
+
+      Concurrency 4 also sets `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=50,43` (an uneven 50/43 layer split across the two pipeline stages), and concurrency 96 lowers `--gpu-memory-utilization` to 0.915.
+
+      **Mooncake store.** The points marked with a segment size run the embedded RDMA store with `P2PHANDSHAKE` metadata, a 4GB `local_buffer_size` and the `MooncakeStoreConnector` that the builder's **Mooncake** option renders. The builder's master and store config use a 100GB segment, which is the default, so raise it to the lane's value only when the node has that much pinned memory to spare. The lane starts the master with no extra flags, where the builder's master command sets `-default_kv_lease_ttl=30000 -eviction_high_watermark_ratio=0.95 -eviction_ratio=0.1`. Set `device_name` and `MC_GID_INDEX` for your RDMA fabric. The three points marked off (16, 24 and 32) run without a KV connector, a Mooncake master or the `MC_*`, `UCX_*` and `VLLM_MOONCAKE_*` variables.
+
+      **Kept out of the preset.** `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`, `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE`, `VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL`, `TILELANG_CLEANUP_TEMP_FILES` and the Hugging Face cache paths are client usage reporting, logging or cache-location controls with no effect on the served model. `--moe-backend auto` is vLLM's default selection and is stated only to match the lane. The lane's fabric device and GID selection and `WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=0` are specific to its cluster. `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` and `VLLM_RPC_TIMEOUT` are not read by the pinned image's `vllm/envs.py`.

+# HY4
+
+vLLM supports `tencent/Hy4-preview` and `tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8` through
+`HYV4ForCausalLM`.
+
+## AMD ROCm graph execution
+
+HY4 on AMD ROCm uses breakable HIP graphs by default, without `torch.compile`.
+No `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` override is required. This keeps graph capture
+enabled for prefill and decode while selecting kernels for the captured batch
+size, including the small-batch MXFP8 linear configurations.
+
+The AMD backbone does not support `torch.compile`. Setting
+`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` does not restore compiler support. Use
+`--enforce-eager` to disable graph execution for debugging.
+
+See [CUDA graphs](../design/cuda_graphs.md) for graph execution modes; the same
+configuration terminology applies to HIP graphs on ROCm.

[Rust][Benchmark] Keep transport failures visible in measured requests (#65284)

Signed-off-by: reidliu41 <reid201711@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: vllm-agent <claw@inferact.ai>

files.patch:
@@ -830,7 +830,7 @@ src/
 - **Enum dispatch** — backend variants instead of trait objects (avoids async trait-object limitations)
 - **Typed SSE deserialization** — `CompletionChunk`/`ChatChunk` structs skip unused JSON fields (cheaper than `serde_json::Value`)
 - **Speculative JSON parse** — SSE handler uses `serde_json::value::RawValue` to detect complete JSON before `\n\n` arrives, improving TTFT/ITL accuracy when TCP segments split
-- **Connection error retry** — automatic retry with backoff on connection reset/timeout/refused (up to 3 attempts)
+- **Measured request semantics** — each workload request is attempted once, matching Python; connection failures are reported rather than retried
 - **Tokenizer verification cache** — server-side token-length verification is cached per model+server pair
 
 ### Behavioral parity with Python

+_PyObject_GC_UnTrack.argtypes = [ctypes.py_object]
+_PyObject_GC_UnTrack.restype = None

+def gc_untrack(obj: _T) -> _T:
+    """Hide a container from the cyclic GC, so that collections skip its
+    elements. Reference counting still frees it.
+
+    Only for containers that can never be part of a reference cycle (e.g. a
+    list of atomic values, or of objects that never refer back to it): a cycle
+    through an untracked container is never collected. Dicts re-track
+    themselves when a tracked value is inserted, so this suits lists.
+    A no-op for objects the GC does not track (e.g. arrays, empty tuples).
+    """
+    if gc.is_tracked(obj):
+        _PyObject_GC_UnTrack(obj)
+    return obj

+    """An empty list that the cyclic GC never traverses (see `gc_untrack`)."""
+    return gc_untrack([])

+    twice: untracking costs ~0.2us per call against ~20ns per element scanned,

     if world_size > torch.accelerator.device_count():
         pytest.skip("Not enough GPUs to run the test.")
     multi_process_parallel(monkeypatch, tp_size, pipeline_parallel_size, test_target)
+
+
+def _order_sensitive_inputs(
+    numel: int, dtype: torch.dtype, world_size: int, seed: int
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Per-rank inputs, shape [numel, world_size], whose sum depends on the
+    order the ranks are accumulated in.
+
+    Each element holds +B, -B and small terms t in a random rank order, with t
+    below the float32 accumulator's resolution at B: adding t to B loses it,
+    cancelling +B and -B first keeps it, and the difference survives the
+    downcast. Ordinary random fp16/bf16 data cannot detect a changed order,
+    because its float32 partial sums are exact.
+    """
+    log2_big, log2_tiny = {
+        torch.float16: (13, -13),
+        torch.bfloat16: (20, -8),
+        torch.float32: (20, -8),
+    }[dtype]
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    big = (torch.rand(numel, generator=gen, dtype=torch.float64) + 1) * 2.0**log2_big
+    tiny = torch.rand(numel, world_size - 2, generator=gen, dtype=torch.float64) + 1
+    sign = torch.randint(0, 2, tiny.shape, generator=gen) * 2 - 1
+    tiny *= sign * 2.0**log2_tiny
+    terms = torch.cat([big[:, None], -big[:, None], tiny], dim=1)
+    order = torch.argsort(torch.rand(numel, world_size, generator=gen), dim=1)
+    return torch.gather(terms, 1, order).to(dtype)
+
+
+@ray.remote(num_gpus=1, max_calls=1)
+def one_and_two_stage_allreduce(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+    tp_size,
+    pp_size,
+    rank,
+    distributed_init_port,
+):
+    with monkeypatch.context() as m:
+        m.delenv("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", raising=False)
+        m.delenv("HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES", raising=False)
+        device = torch.device(f"cuda:{rank}")
+        torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+        init_test_distributed_environment(tp_size, pp_size, rank, distributed_init_port)
+        fa = get_tp_group().device_communicator.ca_comm
+        assert fa is not None and not fa.disabled, "custom all-reduce is disabled"
+
+        # Sizes are counts of 16-byte packed elements. They straddle the
+        # 512 KiB 1-stage/2-stage threshold, and all but one leave a remainder
+        # when divided by the world size, giving the last rank a larger part.
+        for dtype, bits in [
+            (torch.float16, torch.int16),
+            (torch.bfloat16, torch.int16),
+            (torch.float32, torch.int32),
+        ]:
+            for packed in [1021, 32771, 65536, 262139]:
+                numel = packed * (16 // torch.empty((), dtype=dtype).element_size())
+                case = f"{dtype}, {packed * 16} bytes"
+
+                ints = torch.randint(
+                    -8, 9, (numel, tp_size), generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+                ).to(dtype)
+                exact = ints.sum(dim=1).to(device)
+                inputs = _order_sensitive_inputs(numel, dtype, tp_size, seed=packed)
+                outs = {}
+                for algo in ["1stage", "2stage"]:
+                    m.setenv("VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO", algo)
+                    summed = fa.all_reduce(
+                        ints[:, rank].contiguous().to(device), registered=False
+                    )
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(summed, exact, rtol=0, atol=0)
+                    outs[algo] = fa.all_reduce(
+                        inputs[:, rank].contiguous().to(device), registered=False
+                    )
+                torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+
+                differ = outs["1stage"].view(bits) != outs["2stage"].view(bits)
+                assert not differ.any(), (
+                    f"{case}: 2-stage differs from 1-stage in "
+                    f"{int(differ.sum())}/{numel} elements"
+                )

+def device_memory_info(device: torch.types.Device = None) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Free and total device memory in bytes, like
+    `torch.accelerator.get_memory_info`, with the free memory corrected on
+    integrated GPUs.
+
+    On UMA (Unified Memory Architecture) platforms where CPU and GPU share
+    physical memory (e.g. GH200, DGX Spark, Jetson Orin), cudaMemGetInfo
+    underreports free memory because it does not account for reclaimable OS
+    memory (page cache, buffers), which a device allocation does reclaim.
+    psutil reports the true available memory there.
+    https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-for-tegra-appnote/#estimating-total-allocatable-device-memory-on-an-integrated-gpu-device
+    """
+    free_memory, total_memory = torch.accelerator.get_memory_info(device)
+    index = torch.device(device).index if device is not None else None
+    if current_platform.is_integrated_gpu(index):
+        free_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().available
+    return free_memory, total_memory
+

+def _remote_scheduler(max_num_seqs: int, max_num_inflight_kv_loads: int):

+def test_inflight_kv_loads_start_while_batch_full():
+    """With --max-num-inflight-kv-loads, loads start while the running batch is
+    full, up to the cap, and a finished load counts until its request runs."""
+    scheduler, block_size = _remote_scheduler(
+        max_num_seqs=1, max_num_inflight_kv_loads=2
+    )
+    local = create_request(block_size=block_size, num_tokens=block_size)
+    scheduler.add_request(local)
+    scheduler_output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert scheduler.running == [local]
+
+    remote = [
+        create_request(
+            block_size=block_size, num_tokens=block_size * 3, do_remote_prefill=True
+        )
+        for _ in range(4)
+    ]
+    for request in remote:
+        scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler_output, create_model_runner_output([local]))
+    scheduler_output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert scheduler.running == [local]
+    assert [r.status for r in remote] == [RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS] * 2 + [
+        RequestStatus.WAITING
+    ] * 2
+    assert list(scheduler.async_kv_waiting) == remote[2:]
+
+    # A finished load holds its blocks until its request runs.
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        scheduler_output,
+        create_model_runner_output([local], finished_recving={remote[0].request_id}),
+    )
+    scheduler_output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert _kv_fetch_stages(scheduler)[1:] == (1, 1)
+    assert remote[2].status == RequestStatus.WAITING
+
+    # The freed slot goes to the finished load, which lets the next one start.
+    scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler_output, create_model_runner_output([local]))
+    scheduler.finish_requests(local.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+    scheduler.schedule()
+    assert scheduler.running == [remote[0]]
+    assert remote[2].status == RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS
+    assert list(scheduler.async_kv_waiting) == remote[3:]

+def test_early_kv_load_does_not_overtake_finished_load():

+    a finished load gets the next free slot."""

+    )

+    scheduler.add_request(local)

+    older, newer = (
+        create_request(
+            block_size=block_size, num_tokens=block_size * 3, do_remote_prefill=True
+        )

+def test_aborted_kv_load_counts_until_transfer_done():
+    """An aborted load keeps its place under the cap while its transfer still
+    writes its blocks, so cancelling loading requests can't exceed the cap."""
+    scheduler, block_size = _remote_scheduler(
+        max_num_seqs=1, max_num_inflight_kv_loads=1
+    )
+    local = create_request(block_size=block_size, num_tokens=block_size)
+    scheduler.add_request(local)
+    scheduler_output = scheduler.schedule()
+    aborted, waiting = (
+        create_request(
+            block_size=block_size, num_tokens=block_size * 3, do_remote_prefill=True
+        )
+        for _ in range(2)
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(aborted)
+    scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler_output, create_model_runner_output([local]))
+    scheduler_output = scheduler.schedule()

+                params_dtype=dtype,
+            )

+                if param.dtype == torch.uint8:
+                    param.data.copy_(torch.randint(0, 256, param.shape))

+    linears = {nvfp4: make_linear(nvfp4) for nvfp4 in (False, True)}
+
+    def run_one(nvfp4, allreduce, num_tokens):
+        linear = None if nvfp4 is None else linears[nvfp4]
+        set_random_seed(42)
+        norm = Qwen3_5RMSNorm(HIDDEN_SIZE, eps=1e-6, reduce_inputs=allreduce).cuda()
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            norm.weight.normal_(mean=0.0, std=0.1)

+        torch.manual_seed(42 + 7)
+        residual = torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+        torch.manual_seed(42 + 1000 + local_rank)

+        # reduces the sum of squares in a different order than FlashInfer's

+            dist = (_fp8_codes(qa.data) - _fp8_codes(ref_q)).abs()
+            sf_mismatch = 0.0
+        if exact:
+            assert dist.max().item() == 0
+            assert sf_mismatch == 0.0
+        else:
+            assert dist.max().item() <= 1
+            assert (dist > 0).float().mean().item() <= 1e-4
+            assert sf_mismatch <= 1e-4
+

+        for num_tokens in (1, 17, 333, FALLBACK_TOKENS):
+            run_one(nvfp4, True, num_tokens)
+        run_one(nvfp4, False, 17)
+    for allreduce in (False, True):
+        run_one(None, allreduce, 17)
+    cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()
+
+
+def test_forward_fused():
+    if current_platform.device_count() < WORLD_SIZE:

+    spawn(
+        _worker,
+        args=(WORLD_SIZE, str(get_open_port())),
+        nprocs=WORLD_SIZE,
+        join=True,
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""TP all-reduce + residual add + Gemma RMSNorm + consumer input quant.
+
+Calls FlashInfer's ``kARResidualRMSNormOut{FP8,FP4}Quant`` patterns directly
+(no torch.compile custom op). The kernel writes the bf16 normed activation
+(GDN's ``in_proj_ba`` reads it) next to the static FP8 / NVFP4 codes; its
+outputs are bitwise identical to FlashInfer AR+norm followed by
+``scaled_fp8_quant`` / ``scaled_fp4_quant``.
+
+Returns None when the fused kernel does not apply (FlashInfer or a supported
+workspace unavailable, or a batch above the workspace budget); the caller
+then runs an explicit all-reduce and the Triton norm-quant.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config.compilation import PassConfig
+from vllm.distributed.device_communicators import flashinfer_all_reduce as fi_ar
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import (
+    get_tensor_model_parallel_rank,
+    get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size,
+    get_tp_group,
+)
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fusion.quant_activation import QuantizedActivation
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import (
+    QuantKey,
+    kNvfp4Dynamic,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import round_up
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# Gemma RMSNorm scales by (1 + weight).
+_GEMMA_WEIGHT_BIAS = 1.0
+
+# Set when the quant workspace cannot be created for this TP group (e.g. the
+# trtllm backend across nodes); get_fi_ar_quant_workspace raises on every call.
+_workspace_unsupported = False
+
+
+def _get_workspace(hidden_states: torch.Tensor, tp_size: int):
+    """The FlashInfer quant workspace if it can take ``hidden_states``, else
+    None."""
+    global _workspace_unsupported
+    if not fi_ar.fi_ar_available or _workspace_unsupported:
+        return None
+    if (
+        not hidden_states.is_cuda
+        or hidden_states.dim() != 2
+        or not hidden_states.is_contiguous()
+        or hidden_states.dtype not in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16)
+    ):
+        return None
+
+    # Same budget as the non-quant AR+norm workspace, which a matching backend
+    # shares with this one.
+    max_size_mb = PassConfig.default_fi_allreduce_fusion_max_size_mb().get(tp_size)
+    if not max_size_mb:
+        return None
+    num_tokens, hidden_size = hidden_states.shape
+    max_token_num = int(max_size_mb * 1024 * 1024) // (
+        hidden_size * hidden_states.element_size()
+    )
+    if num_tokens > max_token_num:
+        return None
+
+    try:
+        workspace = fi_ar.get_fi_ar_quant_workspace(
+            world_size=tp_size,
+            rank=get_tensor_model_parallel_rank(),
+            max_token_num=max_token_num,
+            hidden_dim=hidden_size,
+            dtype=hidden_states.dtype,
+            group=get_tp_group().cpu_group,
+        )
+    except ValueError as e:
+        logger.warning_once("FlashInfer AR+norm+quant disabled: %s", e)
+        _workspace_unsupported = True
+        return None
+    # mnnvl rotates through three Lamport buffers, so less than the whole
+    # budget is usable per call.
+    if workspace is None or not workspace.is_buffer_size_sufficient(
+        tp_size=tp_size,
+        num_tokens=num_tokens,
+        hidden_dim=hidden_size,
+        dtype=hidden_states.dtype,
+    ):
+        return None
+    return workspace
+
+
+def fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm_quant(
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    residual: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    eps: float,
+    scale: torch.Tensor,
+    key: QuantKey,
+) -> tuple[QuantizedActivation, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None:
+    """Fused ``gemma_rms_norm(all_reduce(hidden_states) + residual)`` + quant.
+
+    ``hidden_states`` is the per-rank partial of a row-parallel linear;
+    ``scale`` is the consumer's static FP8 input scale or NVFP4 global scale
+    inverse. Returns the quantized normed activation, the normed activation in
+    ``hidden_states``' dtype, and the new residual (written into the
+    ``hidden_states`` buffer), or None when the fused kernel does not apply.
+    """
+    tp_size = get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
+    workspace = _get_workspace(hidden_states, tp_size)
+    if workspace is None:
+        return None
+
+    flashinfer_comm = fi_ar.flashinfer_comm
+    patterns = flashinfer_comm.AllReduceFusionPattern
+    nvfp4 = key == kNvfp4Dynamic
+    num_tokens, hidden_size = hidden_states.shape
+    norm_out = torch.empty_like(hidden_states)
+    if nvfp4:
+        pattern = patterns.kARResidualRMSNormOutFP4Quant
+        quant_out = torch.empty(
+            (num_tokens, hidden_size // 2),
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            device=hidden_states.device,
+        )
+        # 128x4-swizzled block scales, as scaled_fp4_quant lays them out.
+        scale_out = torch.empty(
+            (round_up(num_tokens, 128), round_up(hidden_size // 16, 4) // 4),
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device=hidden_states.device,
+        ).view(current_platform.fp8_dtype())
+    else:
+        pattern = patterns.kARResidualRMSNormOutFP8Quant
+        quant_out = torch.empty_like(hidden_states, dtype=current_platform.fp8_dtype())
+        scale_out = None
+
+    # use_oneshot=None leaves the one-shot/two-shot choice to FlashInfer, and
+    # the default trigger_completion_at_end=True keeps the trtllm one-shot
+    # kernel from signalling PDL dependents before its output is written.
+    flashinfer_comm.allreduce_fusion(
+        input=hidden_states,
+        workspace=workspace,
+        pattern=pattern,
+        launch_with_pdl=True,
+        residual_in=residual,
+        residual_out=hidden_states,
+        norm_out=norm_out,
+        quant_out=quant_out,
+        scale_out=scale_out,
+        rms_gamma=weight,
+        rms_eps=eps,
+        scale_factor=scale,
+        layout_code=flashinfer_comm.QuantizationSFLayout.SWIZZLED_128x4,
+        use_oneshot=None,
+        fp32_acc=True,
+        weight_bias=_GEMMA_WEIGHT_BIAS,
+    )
+    qa = QuantizedActivation(
+        data=quant_out,
+        scale=scale_out if nvfp4 else scale,
+        orig_dtype=hidden_states.dtype,
+        orig_shape=hidden_states.shape,
+        quant_key=key,
+    )
+    return qa, norm_out, hidden_states

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+import json
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.tool_parsers.schema_types import convert_value, parameter_types
+
+_NULLABLE_STR = {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]}
+_INT_OR_STR = {"anyOf": [{"type": "integer"}, {"type": "string"}]}
+_BODY = '{\n  "version": "1.4.0",\n  "build": 7\n}'
+_DEFS = {
+    "S": {"type": "string"},
+    "C": {"allOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/C"}, {"type": "string"}]},
+    # Each def references the next one twice: 2**60 paths without memoization.
+    **{f"D{i}": {"anyOf": [{"$ref": f"#/$defs/D{i + 1}"}] * 2} for i in range(60)},
+    "D60": {"type": "string"},
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("schema", "raw", "expected"),
+    [
+        # plain string and non-string types: unchanged
+        ({"type": "string"}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"type": "integer"}, "1.10", 1.1),
+        # schemas that admit a string keep the raw text...
+        (_NULLABLE_STR, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        (_NULLABLE_STR, "1984", "1984"),
+        (_NULLABLE_STR, _BODY, _BODY),
+        (_NULLABLE_STR, '"q"', '"q"'),
+        ({"oneOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]}, "true", "true"),
+        ({"type": ["string", "null"]}, "1984", "1984"),
+        ({"enum": ["1.10", "2.0"]}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"const": "1.10"}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"$ref": "#/$defs/S"}, "1984", "1984"),
+        ({"allOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/S"}, {"description": "d"}]}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"$ref": "#/$defs/C"}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"allOf": [_NULLABLE_STR, {"type": "string"}]}, "null", "null"),
+        ({"$ref": "#/$defs/D0"}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        (_INT_OR_STR, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"type": ["number", "string"]}, "true", "true"),
+        # ...unless the value decodes to another admitted type
+        (_NULLABLE_STR, "null", None),
+        (_INT_OR_STR, "25", 25),
+        ({"type": ["number", "string"]}, "25", 25),
+        ({"enum": [1, "a"]}, "1", 1),
+        ({"type": ["number", "string"], "enum": [1, "x"]}, "1", 1),
+        ({"anyOf": [{"type": "number"}, {"type": "string"}], "enum": [1, "x"]}, "1", 1),
+        ({"allOf": [{"type": ["number", "string"]}, {"enum": [1, "x"]}]}, "1", 1),
+        # no string admitted, or no type information: decode as before
+        ({"anyOf": [{"type": "number"}, {"type": "null"}]}, "1.10", 1.1),
+        ({"description": "untyped"}, "25", 25),
+        ({"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {}]}, "25", 25),
+    ],
+)
+def test_convert_value(schema, raw, expected):
+    params = {
+        "$defs": _DEFS,
+        "properties": {"v": schema},
+        "additionalProperties": schema,
+    }
+    props, extra = parameter_types([{"name": "f", "parameters": params}])["f"]
+    for allowed in props["v"], extra:
+        assert convert_value(raw, allowed, json.loads) == expected
